definition_zh: 几乎；差不多；将近；差一点
definition_en: not quite, but very close to something in amount or degree
core_image: 杯中水快到杯口但还差一点
scene: 桌上有一只杯子，水已经快到杯口，但还差一点。 The glass is almost full.
sceneCN: 这里 almost 是「几乎」（第 1 个义项：非常接近但尚未完全）；句意为杯子几乎满了。

senses.title: Nearly an amount or degree
senses.titleCN: 几乎达到某个数量或程度
senses.definition: very close to an amount or a degree but not reaching it
senses.definitionCN: 非常接近某个数量或程度，但尚未达到
senses.example: Almost all the seats were taken.
senses.exampleCN: 几乎所有的座位都被占了。
senses.why: All plus most means reaching the greatest part, so the word first marks a near total.
senses.whyCN: all 加 most 意为达到最大部分，所以这个词先标记接近全部。

senses.title: Nearly happening
senses.definition: very close to an event that did not happen
senses.definitionCN: 非常接近一件未发生的事
senses.example: I almost fell on the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 我在冰上差点摔倒。
senses.why: The same nearness was applied to events, where it means only a little kept something from happening.
senses.whyCN: 同样的接近用在事件上，就表示只差一点就发生了。

intro.en: The recorded history of almost is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 almost 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: The old form joined eall, all, with maest, most.
items.cn: 古形式把表示全部的 eall 与表示最多的 maest 结合。

items.en: Middle English smoothed the compound into almost.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个复合词简化成 almost。

items.en: English used almost for what falls just short.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪用 almost 指只差一点的事物。

items.en: Later it described nearness in time and in quality.
items.cn: 后来它也形容时间与性质上的接近。

items.en: Today it is one of the commonest adverbs in English.
items.cn: 今天它是英语里最常用的副词之一。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The superlative word that ends the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个词的后半部分，表示最多。

entries.definition: The word for the whole amount.
entries.definitionCN: 表示全部数量的词。

entries.definition: The adverb for mainly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，表示主要地。

entries.definition: It stresses coming close to an amount.
entries.definitionCN: 强调接近某个数量。

entries.definition: It stresses a rough figure rather than reaching it.
entries.definitionCN: 强调大致数目，而非达到。

entries.definition: It stresses a loose estimate.
entries.definitionCN: 强调粗略的估计。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded form, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: all plus most means as much as possible: almost is nearly the whole amount.
normal.cn: all 加 most 意为尽可能多：almost 就是几乎达到全部。

normal.en: The same family also gives most and all.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 most 与 all。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase almost all.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「几乎所有」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of almost in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 almost 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: not quite, but very close to something in amount or degree.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「几乎」时用它。

abstract.en: Picture water in a glass rising close to the rim but not reaching it.
abstract.cn: 想象杯中水快到杯口但还差一点。

abstract.en: The same picture can be literal in one sentence and figurative in another.
abstract.cn: 同一幅画面在一句里可以是字面意思，在另一句里可以是比喻。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

examples.en: Almost all the seats were taken.
examples.cn: 几乎所有的座位都被占了。

examples.en: I almost fell on the ice.
examples.cn: 我在冰上差点摔倒。

examples.en: Dinner is almost ready.
examples.cn: 晚饭快好了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奥尔莫斯特」——杯里的水快满还差一点：几乎

root: almost 来自古英语 eall「全部」与 maest「最多」的结合，中古英语简化成 almost；十四世纪用它表示只差一点，后来也形容时间与性质上的接近，今天是最常用的副词之一。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of almost grows from one core image: water in a glass rising close to the rim but not reaching it.
sensesIntro.cn: almost 的各个义项都从同一个核心意象生长出来：杯中水快到杯口但还差一点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water in a glass rising close to the rim but not reaching it
core.cn: 核心意象：杯中水快到杯口但还差一点

branches.en: Sense 01 covers the most literal use: Nearly an amount or degree.
branches.cn: 义项 01 覆盖最字面的用法：几乎达到某个数量或程度。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a wider everyday use: Nearly happening.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更宽泛的日常用法：差一点发生。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the two main uses: Nearly an amount or degree / Nearly happening.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖两个主要用法：几乎达到某个数量或程度、差一点发生。

branches.en: Sense 02 covers a further use: Nearly happening.
branches.cn: 义项 02 覆盖更靠后的一种用法：差一点发生。

branches.en: Sense 01 · 02 covers the outer edge of the meaning: Nearly an amount or degree / Nearly happening.
branches.cn: 义项 01 · 02 覆盖意义的边缘：几乎达到某个数量或程度、差一点发生。

intro.en: almost can be split into the parts below, which also connect it to common English patterns.
intro.cn: almost 可以按下面的成分拆开，这些成分也把它与常见的英语构词方式连起来。

latinIntro.en: No recorded Latin cognate is securely attached to this word, so the list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠记录的拉丁同族词可以系在这个词上，因此该列表留空。

items.exampleCN: 它是 almost 的前半部分。
它是 almost 的后半部分。

items.example: It marks a plural noun in English.
It marks the past tense or a completed state.
items.exampleCN: 它标记过去时或已完成的状态。

items.example: It forms the present participle of a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成动词的现在分词。

items.example: It turns an adjective into an adverb.
It names the doer of an action.
items.exampleCN: 它指做某动作的人或物。

items.example: It turns an adjective into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成表状态的名词。

definition_zh: 主要地；大部分；通常；几乎全部
definition_en: for the greatest part of a group or amount; in most cases or most of the time; and almost entirely
core_image: 一只盘子里大半装着米饭，边角只留几样小菜
scene: 傍晚的自助餐厅里，长桌大半已经空了，只有靠窗那几盘菜还被夹得七零八落。 By eight the buffet was quiet, and the trays that were mostly empty had been stacked by the door.
sceneCN: 这里是「大半、大部分」（第 1 个义项：指一个整体中的多数部分）；句意为到八点时自助餐区已经安静下来，那些大半空了的托盘被叠在门边。图中可辨识物件：长餐台、成摞的托盘、靠窗的菜盘。

pos.zh: 主要地；大部分；通常；几乎全部

derivatives.zh: 与 mostly 同源的基础词，去掉副词后缀 -ly 即得，义为「最多的；大多数的」
由古英语 eall（全部）与 māst（最多）缩合而成，义为「几乎」，与 most 同源
由古英语 ūt（向外）加 most 构成，义为「最远的；极度的」

senses.title: The greatest share of a group
senses.definition: applying to the greater number of people or things in a group
senses.definitionCN: 适用于一个群体中数量占多数的人或物
senses.example: The guests at the wedding were mostly relatives from her side.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼上的宾客多半是她这边的亲戚。
senses.why: The word is built on the Old English superlative māst, the greatest share, so its first duty is to report how a whole divides rather than to name a frequency.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在古英语最高级 māst（最大的份额）上，所以它首先管的是「一个整体怎么分」，而不是说事情多久发生一次。

senses.title: In most cases, as a habit
senses.definition: happening on most occasions, though not on every one
senses.definitionCN: 在多数场合都会发生，但并非每一次
senses.example: He mostly takes the early train and reads on the way.
senses.exampleCN: 他通常坐早班车，在路上看书。
senses.why: Once the word could mark the larger part of anything, it could also mark the larger part of a routine, which is how a share of a group turned into a habitual frequency.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能标出任何事物里较大的那部分，它也就能标出日常习惯里较大的那部分，群体份额就这样长成了习惯性的频率。

senses.title: Nearly the whole of an amount
senses.definition: covering the largest part of a quantity or substance, with only a small remainder
senses.definitionCN: 占去数量或物质的最大部分，只剩下很少一点
senses.example: The bottle in the shed is mostly rainwater.
senses.exampleCN: 棚子里那瓶装的几乎全是雨水。
senses.why: Measuring a substance leaves a visible remainder, so the same superlative sense reads as a near total: the greatest share of a bottle is almost the bottle, and the rest is an exception.
senses.whyCN: 给一样东西计量时总会剩下一小点，于是同一个最高级的意思读成了「接近全部」：一只瓶子里的最大份额就是几乎整瓶，剩下那点只是例外。

intro.en: Mostly is an Old English superlative turned into an adverb: most, the greatest share, plus the ending -ly, which says in what manner a statement holds.
intro.cn: mostly 是古英语最高级加副词词尾构成的词：most 指最大的份额，-ly 表示一句话以什么方式成立。

items.en: Māst was the superlative of micel, great, and it named the greatest amount or the greatest share of a group.
items.cn: māst 是 micel（大的）的最高级，指最大的数量，或一个群体中最大的份额。

items.en: The ending -līce came from līc, body or form, and it turned an adjective into an adverb meaning in the manner of something; in English it settled as -ly.
items.cn: -līce 这个词尾出自 līc（身体、形貌），把形容词变成表示「以……方式」的副词；进入英语后固定为 -ly。

items.en: Middle English joined most and -ly into mostli, an adverb reporting what holds for the greater number of cases.
items.cn: 中古英语把 most 与 -ly 合成 mostli，用作副词，表示对多数情形都成立。

items.en: By the fifteenth century mostly was common in the sense of for the greatest part, and it stood beside almost, which had grown from all and most.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，mostly 已常见，意为「大部分」；它与由 all 与 most 合成的 almost 并列使用。

items.en: Modern English keeps three readings: a share of a group, a habitual frequency, and a near total in amount, and dictionaries list them as separate senses.
items.cn: 现代英语保留三种读法：群体中的份额、习惯性的频率、数量上接近全部；词典把它们分列为不同义项。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the Old English words that share the most element; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of majority and frequency.
note.cn: 形近组收与 most 共用词素的古英语词与英语词；近义组收表示多数与频率的副词。

entries.definition: The greatest amount, or the greater number of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 最大的数量，或一个群体中的多数。

entries.definition: Not quite, but very nearly.
entries.definitionCN: 差一点，但非常接近。

entries.definition: Farthest out, or greatest in degree.
entries.definitionCN: 最远的，或程度最大的。

entries.definition: Ranking first in importance or position.
entries.definitionCN: 在重要性或位置上居首的。

entries.definition: More than anything else, or for the greater part.
entries.definitionCN: 首要地，或大部分情况下。

entries.definition: To a great extent.
entries.definitionCN: 在很大程度上。

entries.definition: In most cases or on most occasions.
entries.definitionCN: 多数情况下，或多数场合。

entries.definition: Above all; mostly but not only.
entries.definitionCN: 首先；主要是，但不只是。

normalIntro.en: The word is one Old English superlative plus one adverbial ending, and everything about it follows from the idea of the greatest share.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一个古英语最高级加一个副词词尾，它的全部用法都从「最大份额」这个想法里长出来。

normal.en: Most is the superlative of great, so mostly begins with the idea of the greatest share, not with a vague idea of many.
normal.cn: most 是 great 的最高级，所以 mostly 的起点是「最大份额」，而不是笼统的「很多」。

normal.en: -ly comes from an Old English word for body or form, and it turns an adjective into a statement about manner.
normal.cn: -ly 出自古英语里表示身体或形貌的词，它把形容词变成说明「方式」的词。

normal.en: Almost is all plus most, a near total, and it sits beside mostly in the same family of degree words.
normal.cn: almost 是 all 加 most，表示接近全部，它与 mostly 并排站在同一族程度词里。

normal.en: Weather reports say mostly sunny because the forecast covers most of a region and most of a day, not every square metre or every minute.
normal.cn: 天气预报说 mostly sunny，因为预报覆盖的是一个地区的大部分和一天的大部分，而不是每一平方米、每一分钟。

normal.en: Mostly because names the leading reason among several, which is the same share logic applied to causes instead of things.
normal.cn: mostly because 指几个原因里最主要的那个，这正是把「份额」的逻辑从事物挪到了原因。

abstract.en: Picture a plate where rice fills most of the surface and two small side dishes take the corners.
abstract.cn: 想象一只盘子，米饭占去大半个盘面，两样小菜只占边角。

abstract.en: A word for the largest share keeps the minority visible: mostly means not entirely, so the rest is still there.
abstract.cn: 一个表示最大份额的词始终让少数派可见：mostly 意为「并非全部」，剩下的部分仍在。

abstract.en: Because it measures shares rather than absolutes, mostly fits sentences that report, estimate and predict, from weather to polls.
abstract.cn: 因为它衡量的是份额而不是绝对，mostly 特别适合报告、估计和预测的句子，从天气到民调都是。

examples.en: The trays on the counter were mostly empty by eight.
examples.cn: 到八点时，柜台上的托盘大半已经空了。

examples.en: She mostly works from home on Fridays.
examples.cn: 她周五通常在家工作。

examples.en: The report is mostly accurate, with two figures out of date.
examples.cn: 这份报告大体准确，只有两个数字过时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫斯特里」——大半时间都在忙，只剩一点才歇；记住 mostly 是大半、通常、几乎全部。

root: 古英语 māst（最多的，micel 的最高级）加副词词尾 -līce（后作 -ly）构成 mostli，中古英语起意为「大部分」；同族词有 most、almost、utmost、foremost，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the largest share; the senses divide into a share of a group, a habitual frequency, and a near total in amount.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是最大份额；义项分出群体中的多数、习惯性的频率，以及数量上的接近全部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate where one dish covers most of the surface and small portions sit at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只盘子，一样菜占去大半，边上只留几小份。

branches.en: a tray with a few crumbs left on it
branches.cn: 只剩几点碎屑的托盘

branches.en: a hall where most seats are taken
branches.cn: 大半座位已坐了人的礼堂

branches.en: the early train taken on every working morning
branches.cn: 每个工作日早晨都坐的那班早车

branches.en: a bottle holding water with a thin layer of oil on top
branches.cn: 瓶里几乎全是水，只浮着一薄层油

branches.en: one adverb covering both how often a thing happens and how much of it there is
branches.cn: 同一个副词，既管事情多久发生一次，也管一样东西占了多少

intro.en: One Old English superlative, one adverbial ending and the English words built from them hold the entry together.
intro.cn: 一个古英语最高级、一个副词词尾，以及由它们构成的英语词，把这个词条撑了起来。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded: mostly belongs to the Old English stock of degree words, and its relatives are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录：mostly 属于古英语的程度词系统，其亲属词来自日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 冰；冰块；冰淇淋；结冰
definition_en: frozen water, or to cover something with a layer of frozen water
core_image: 水在冷里站住不动了
scene: 冬天清晨的湖边一步一滑。 The lake was covered with thin ice.
sceneCN: 这里 ice 是「冰」（第 1 个义项：水冻结成的固体）；句意：湖面覆盖着薄冰。

derivatives.zh: 冰冷的；多冰的；加形容词后缀

senses.title: Frozen water
senses.definition: water that has frozen hard
senses.definitionCN: 水冻结成的坚硬固体
senses.example: The pond froze and the children slid on the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 池塘结冰，孩子们在冰上滑行。
senses.why: Cold stops water from moving; the stopping itself becomes a thing you can touch.
senses.whyCN: 寒冷让水停止流动，这种「停住」本身成了可以触摸的东西。

senses.title: Ice cream or iced drinks
senses.definition: a frozen sweet dessert, or drinks served very cold
senses.definitionCN: 冰冻甜点或加冰的饮品
senses.example: Two cones of ice, please.
senses.exampleCN: 请来两个冰淇淋蛋筒。
senses.why: The frozen water is sweetened and served: the substance becomes a treat.
senses.whyCN: 冰冻的水加糖上桌：物质变成了甜点。

senses.title: A cold manner
senses.definition: coldness in a person's manner or welcome
senses.definitionCN: 态度或接待中的冷淡
senses.example: Her answer was delivered with ice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的回答带着冷冰冰的腔调。
senses.why: Physical coldness maps onto emotional distance: a chill you can feel in a voice.
senses.whyCN: 身体的冷映射到情感的距离：语气里能感到寒意。

senses.title: To freeze or chill
senses.definition: to cover with ice, to chill, or to coat with icing
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖冰层、冰镇或涂糖霜
senses.example: The roads iced over during the night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里路面结了冰。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb: ice acts on things, on drinks and even on cakes.
senses.whyCN: 名词转动词：冰作用于物体、饮料甚至蛋糕。

senses.title: Diamonds in slang
senses.definition: diamonds, in informal slang
senses.definitionCN: 俚语中指钻石
senses.example: The rapper wore ice on every finger.
senses.exampleCN: 那个说唱歌手每根手指都戴着钻石。
senses.why: Diamonds sparkle cold and clear, so slang borrowed the frozen stone image.
senses.whyCN: 钻石冷冽清澈，俚语便借用了这块「冻住的石头」的意象。

intro.en: Ice is an Old English word, is or isen, of Germanic origin, related to Old High German is. Its root beyond Germanic is uncertain, but the word has never left English everyday speech.
intro.cn: ice 是古英语词 is 或 isen，属日耳曼源，与古高地德语 is 同源；日耳曼之外的词根不确定，但它从未离开过英语日常用语。

items.en: The Germanic root gives Dutch ijs and German Eis; the deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼词根给出荷兰语 ijs、德语 Eis；更深的来源不确定。

items.en: Old English is meant ice; the compound isen, to make of ice, appears in early texts.
items.cn: 古英语 is 指冰；复合形式 isen「用冰制作」见于早期文本。

items.en: Middle English is grew compounds like is-bred, ice-bright, in poetry.
items.cn: 中古英语 is 在诗歌中长出 is-bred「冰亮」等复合词。

items.en: Modern English spelled it ice and built the family: icy, iceberg, ice cream.
items.cn: 现代英语定拼为 ice，构建词族：icy、iceberg、ice cream。

items.en: The verb ice and the slang sense for diamonds grew in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 动词 ice 与指钻石的俚语义在十九二十世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the ice family and one false friend. The meaning group compares cold words.
note.cn: 形近组收录 ice 词族与一个假朋友；词义组比较表示寒冷的词。

entries.definition: very cold or covered with ice.
entries.definitionCN: 冰冷的。本词的形容词。

entries.definition: the passage between seats. It sounds the same but means a walkway.
entries.definitionCN: 过道。发音相同，却指座位间的通道。

entries.definition: a huge floating mass of ice.
entries.definitionCN: 冰山。ice 加 berg 的复合词。

entries.definition: thin frozen moisture on surfaces, not a solid sheet.
entries.definitionCN: 霜。表面的薄冰晶，不是整块冰。

entries.definition: soft frozen flakes falling from the sky.

entries.definition: hard pellets of ice falling during storms.

normalIntro.en: These hooks play on the sound of aisle, the break the ice idiom and the icy family.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用与 aisle 的同音、break the ice 惯用语及 icy 词族。

normal.en: ice sounds like aisle but means frozen water; picture the letter i standing on ice.
normal.cn: ice 与 aisle 同音，但指冻住的水；想象字母 i 站在冰上。

normal.en: break the ice: the first joke cracks the frozen silence.
normal.cn: break the ice：第一个笑话敲裂了冻结的沉默。

normal.en: icy turns the noun cold and slippery.
normal.cn: icy 把名词变得又冷又滑。

normal.en: on ice means stored or postponed; put the plan on ice.

normal.en: Slang ice means diamonds: the coldest sparkle.

abstract.en: One image: a glass of water gone still and hard overnight.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：一夜之间那杯水静止变硬。

abstract.en: Ice is water with time stopped inside it.
abstract.cn: 冰是内部时间被冻结的水。

abstract.en: Feel the range: a drink, a pond, a stare, a diamond.
abstract.cn: 感受范围：一杯饮料、一个池塘、一个眼神、一颗钻石。

examples.en: The bartender dropped an ice cube into the glass.
examples.cn: 调酒师往杯里放了一块冰。

examples.en: She skated across the frozen ice.

examples.en: The winter storm iced the power lines.
examples.cn: 冬季风暴让电线结了冰。

root: 古英语 is「冰」，日耳曼语词根，与荷兰语 ijs、德语 Eis 同源；更深来源不确定。现代英语派生 icy、iceberg 等，动词与俚语义为近代发展。

sensesIntro.en: Ice is frozen water first, then a frozen treat, then the chill in a manner, a verb of freezing and chilling, and slang for diamonds.
sensesIntro.cn: ice 先是冻住的水，再是冰冻的甜点、态度里的寒意、冻结与冰镇的动词，最后是钻石的俚语。

core.en: Water stopped by cold, made into something you can touch and feel.
core.cn: 被寒冷停住的水，变成可触摸可感知之物。

branches.en: WATER SOLID: the pond, the cube, the sheet.
branches.cn: 固态水：池塘、冰块、冰面。

branches.en: TREAT: ice cream and iced drinks.
branches.cn: 甜点：冰淇淋与加冰饮料。

branches.en: MANNER: a greeting served with ice.
branches.cn: 态度：冷冰冰的接待。

branches.en: ACTION: roads iced over, cakes iced white.
branches.cn: 动作：路面结冰、蛋糕敷上白霜。

branches.en: JEWELS: slang ice for diamonds.
branches.cn: 珠宝：俚语 ice 指钻石。

intro.en: Ice builds a wide compound family: iceberg, ice cream, ice cube, and the adjective icy with its adverb and noun.
intro.cn: ice 构成庞大的复合词族：iceberg、ice cream、ice cube，以及形容词 icy 及其副词与名词。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁同源词一栏留空；该词族属日耳曼语，拉丁语 glacies 并无亲缘。

definition_zh: 顺序；次序；命令；订单；目（生物分类）；秩序；修会；勋章；议事规则
definition_en: the arrangement of things in a sequence, a command, or a rank in biological classification
core_image: 一队人按身高排成一行，队首的人手里拿着写有编号的名单
scene: 火车站的值班员按出发时间把列车排成一条队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次。 At the station the dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure, and passengers followed that sequence to find their own service.
sceneCN: 这里 order 是「顺序、次序」（第 1 个义项：事物按先后排列的方式）；句意：值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列，旅客照着这个顺序找自己的车次；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 顺序；次序；秩序；命令；订单；目（生物分类）；修会；勋章

derivatives.zh: 普通的（同出拉丁 ordo 词根）

senses.title: A sequence of things
senses.definition: the way things are arranged one after another, especially according to time, size or importance
senses.definitionCN: 事物按时间、大小或重要性一个接一个排列的方式
senses.example: The dispatcher arranged the trains in the order of departure.
senses.exampleCN: 值班员按出发时间把列车排成队列。
senses.why: Latin ordo first meant a row of threads in a loom, then a row of any kind; a sequence is literally a row read from one end.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 ordo 最初指织机上一排经线，后指任何一排；所谓顺序，字面上就是从一端读过去的一排。

senses.title: A command given to someone
senses.definition: an instruction that must be obeyed, especially one given by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 必须服从的指示，尤指由权威给出的指示
senses.example: The captain gave the order to close the gates.
senses.exampleCN: 队长下令关闭大门。
senses.why: A command is what puts others into an order: the word names both the arrangement and the act of imposing it, which is why a military order and a neat row share one term.
senses.whyCN: 命令就是让别人进入某种次序：这个词既指排列，也指强加排列的动作，因此军令与整齐的一行共用一个词。

senses.title: A purchase request
senses.definition: a request for goods or food to be supplied, or the goods so requested
senses.definitionCN: 要求供应商品或食物的请求，或如此要求的货物
senses.example: She placed an order for two hundred copies.
senses.exampleCN: 她订购了两百册。
senses.why: Commerce extended the word from arrangement to instruction: an order tells a supplier what to arrange and in what quantity.
senses.whyCN: 商业把这个词从排列延伸到指示：订单告诉供货者要安排什么、数量多少。

senses.title: The taxonomic rank order
senses.definition: the rank below class and above family in biological classification
senses.definitionCN: 生物分类中位于纲之下、科之上的阶元
senses.example: The order contains twelve families of beetles.
senses.exampleCN: 这个目包含十二个甲虫科。
senses.why: Taxonomy used the Latin word for a row: an order is a row of families, read in one direction down the hierarchy.
senses.whyCN: 分类学用了这个意为「一排」的拉丁词：一个目就是一排科，沿层级往一个方向读下去。

senses.title: Social or public order
senses.definition: the condition in which rules are obeyed and normal activity can continue
senses.definitionCN: 规则得到遵守、正常活动得以继续的状态
senses.example: The police restored order after the march.
senses.exampleCN: 游行之后警方恢复了秩序。
senses.why: The abstract sense generalizes the row: when everyone is in their place, the whole is in order, and the word names that condition rather than any particular row.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把「一排」一般化：当人人各在其位，整体就有秩序，这个词命名的正是那种状态，而非某一特定行列。

senses.title: A religious order
senses.definition: a body of monks, nuns or friars living under one rule, such as the Franciscans
senses.definitionCN: 遵同一会规生活的修士、修女或托钵僧团体，如方济各会
senses.example: The order ran the hospital for three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个修会经营了那所医院三百年。
senses.why: A religious order is a body ordered by a rule; the word names both the community and the discipline that holds it together.
senses.whyCN: 修会是一个按会规排序的团体；这个词既指群体，也指维系群体的那套纪律。

senses.title: An honorary order or decoration
senses.definition: a society of people honoured for service, or the decoration that marks membership
senses.definitionCN: 因功绩受表彰者组成的团体，或标记成员身份的勋章
senses.example: He was admitted to the order for public service.
senses.exampleCN: 他因公共服务被授予该勋位。
senses.why: The sense grew from rank: an order is a graded body of members, and the medal is the visible mark of one's place in it.
senses.whyCN: 这一义由「等级」生长出来：勋位是一个分级的成员团体，勋章则是个人在其中的位置可见的标记。

senses.title: A procedural point in a meeting
senses.definition: a question raised about whether the rules of procedure are being followed, as in a point of order
senses.definitionCN: 关于议事规则是否得到遵守而提出的问题，如程序问题
senses.example: A member raised a point of order before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 表决之前有成员提出了程序问题。
senses.why: Meetings run by rules, and the rules are themselves an order; raising a point of order is asking whether the meeting is still following its own arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 会议依规则进行，而规则本身即是一种秩序；提出程序问题就是问会议是否仍遵守自己的安排。

senses.title: Order of magnitude
senses.definition: a class of scale in which one value is about ten times another, used for rough comparison
senses.definitionCN: 一个值约为另一个值的十倍的尺度等级，用于粗略比较
senses.example: The cost rose by an order of magnitude.
senses.exampleCN: 成本上升了一个数量级。
senses.why: Here order is a step in a graded series: each step multiplies by ten, so the word names a rung rather than a sequence of items.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 order 是分级系列中的一级：每一级乘以十，因此这个词命名的是一级台阶，而不是一串物件。

senses.title: The classical orders of architecture
senses.definition: one of the recognized styles of column and entablature, such as Doric or Corinthian
senses.definitionCN: 多立克、科林斯等被承认的柱与檐部样式之一
senses.example: The facade mixes two architectural orders on one level.
senses.exampleCN: 这面外墙在同一层混用了两种柱式。
senses.why: Vitruvius used ordo for the due arrangement of parts, and the word became the name of each fixed arrangement of column and capital.
senses.whyCN: 维特鲁威用 ordo 指各部分的合宜安排，这个词后来成为柱与柱头每一种固定搭配的名称。

intro.en: Order comes from Latin ordo 'row, rank, arrangement', a third-declension noun whose deeper origin is disputed. It entered English through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: order 来自拉丁 ordo「一排、等级、安排」，是第三变格法名词，其更深来源有争议。该词经古法语进入英语。年代为约数。

items.en: Ordo meant a row, especially a row of threads in a loom, then a rank or an arrangement. The physical row is the oldest image.
items.cn: ordo 指一排，尤其织机上的一排经线，后指等级或安排。物理的一排是最古老的意象。

items.en: The noun is linked to ordiri 'to begin, to lay out a warp'; the connection is accepted, though the verb's own origin is debated.
items.cn: 该名词与 ordiri「开始、铺开经线」相关；这一联系一般认为是成立的，但动词本身的来源仍有争论。

items.en: Old French ordre brought the word into English, where it covered both a row and a command by the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 ordre 把该词带入英语，到 13 世纪已兼指一排与命令。

items.en: The medieval church used order for the ranks of clergy, and the phrase religious order fixed the sense of a community under one rule.
items.cn: 中世纪教会用 order 指神职等级，religious order 一语则固定了「同一会规下的团体」这一义。

items.en: Linnaeus gave order a place in his hierarchy in the eighteenth century, between class and family.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪给 order 在层级中安排了位置，位于纲与科之间。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link between ordo and ordiri is generally accepted, but the pre-Latin origin of both is unsettled, so Indo-European forms offered for them are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ordo 与 ordiri 的联系一般认为是成立的，但二者在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates the many English words that descend from ordo; group two compares words of neighbouring meaning.
note.cn: 第一组区分源自 ordo 的众多英语词；第二组比较意思相邻的词。

entries.definition: A number that marks position in a series, such as first or tenth, from ordinalis. It names a place, not a command.
entries.definitionCN: 标记序列位置的数词，如第一、第十，出自 ordinalis。它指位置，不指命令。

entries.definition: Common or usual, from ordinarius 'according to order'. The sense drifted from 'regular' to 'unremarkable'.
entries.definitionCN: 普通、通常的，出自 ordinarius「按次序的」。词义从「合规矩」漂移到「不出奇」。

entries.definition: A decree or regulation, from ordinare 'to arrange'. It is a law that arranges conduct, not a sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 法令或条例，出自 ordinare「安排」。它是安排行为的法规，不是顺序。

entries.definition: To confer holy orders or to decree, from ordinare. It names an authoritative act, not an arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 授予圣职或颁布，出自 ordinare。它指权威性的行为，而非排列。

entries.definition: A series in which one thing follows another, from sequi 'to follow'. It stresses succession, while order can also mean a command or a rank.
entries.definitionCN: 一物接一物形成的系列，出自 sequi「跟随」。它强调接续，而 order 还可指命令或阶元。

entries.definition: The way items are placed relative to one another. It is the result, while order can be the principle behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 各物彼此的摆放方式。它是结果，order 则可以是背后的原则。

entries.definition: A directive from an authority. It matches one branch of order but not the sequence branch.
entries.definitionCN: 权威发出的指示。它对应 order 的一支，而不对应顺序那一支。

entries.definition: A position in a graded scale, as in taxonomic rank. It names the level, while order can name the whole arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 分级尺度中的位置，如分类阶元。它指层级，order 则可指整套安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ordo was a row of threads: order is first a row, then a rule that keeps things in rows.
normal.cn: ordo 原是一排经线：order 先是一排，后指使事物各在其排的规则。

normal.en: The same word gives ordinal, ordinary, ordinance and ordain, all built on ordinare 'to arrange'.
normal.cn: 同一个词给出 ordinal、ordinary、ordinance、ordain，皆基于 ordinare「安排」。

normal.en: In biology the order sits between class and family, one rung of the ladder.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，目位于纲与科之间，是梯子上的一级。

normal.en: A point of order asks whether the meeting is following its own rules.
normal.cn: 程序问题问的是会议是否遵守自己的规则。

normal.en: An order of magnitude is one step of ten, a rung rather than a row.
normal.cn: 数量级是以十为一步的一级，是一级台阶而非一排。

abstract.en: Picture a loom where one wrong thread makes the whole pattern shift.
abstract.cn: 想象一台织机，一根线错了，整个花样就移位。

abstract.en: Picture a queue that stays calm because everyone knows their number.
abstract.cn: 想象一支队伍因为人人知道自己的号而保持平静。

abstract.en: Picture a cabinet whose drawers are labelled by size, each ten times the one before.
abstract.cn: 想象一柜按大小标注的抽屉，每一格是前一格的十倍。

examples.en: The names were read out in the order in which they had been received.
examples.cn: 姓名按收到的先后顺序被念出。

examples.en: The general's order reached the front line before dawn.
examples.cn: 将军的命令在黎明前传到了前线。

examples.en: The two families belong to the same order but different superfamilies.
examples.cn: 这两个科属于同一个目，但属于不同的总科。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「or 或者 + der 得」——或者这样排、或者那样排，总得有个次序 → order 顺序；命令

root: 拉丁 ordo, ordinis「一排、等级、安排」，与 ordiri「铺开经线、开始」相关；更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of order follow the row outward: a sequence, a command that imposes sequence, a purchase, a taxonomic rung, social calm, a ruled community, an honour, a procedural question, a factor of ten and a style of columns.
sensesIntro.cn: order 的十个义项沿着「一排」向外走：顺序、强加顺序的命令、订单、生物阶元、社会安定、守会规的团体、勋位、程序问题、十倍一级、柱式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row read from one end, and the rule that keeps it a row.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一端读过去的一排，以及使它保持成一排的那条规则。

branches.en: THE ROW ITSELF: a sequence of items, a factor of ten, or a fixed arrangement of columns.
branches.cn: 一排本身：一串物件、十倍的级差，或柱子的固定搭配。

branches.en: THE INSTRUCTION: a command and a purchase both tell someone what to arrange.
branches.cn: 指示：命令与订单都在告诉别人该安排什么。

branches.en: THE RANK: an order in taxonomy and an honour both place a member on a graded ladder.
branches.cn: 等级：生物学的目与勋位都把成员放在分级的梯子上。

branches.en: THE RULE: social order and a point of order both concern whether rules are being kept.
branches.cn: 规则：社会秩序与程序问题都关心规则是否被遵守。

branches.en: THE COMMUNITY: a religious order is a body held together by one rule.
branches.cn: 团体：修会是由一条会规维系的群体。

intro.en: Order is a Latin noun that English uses for rows, commands and ranks alike; the common thread is arranged position.
intro.cn: order 是拉丁名词，英语用它同时指行列、命令与等级；共同的线索是「被安排的位置」。

latinIntro.en: Latin ordo yields order, ordinal, ordinary, ordinance and ordain; ordinare 'to arrange' is the verb behind the derived forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ordo 衍生 order、ordinal、ordinary、ordinance、ordain；ordinare「安排」是这些派生形式背后的动词。

items.example: Ordo began as a row of threads.
The verb supplies ordering and ordinance.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 ordering 与 ordinance。

items.example: One word covers the row and the rule.
items.exampleCN: 一个词同时覆盖一排与规则。
ordinary 的词义漂移到「不出奇」。

items.example: An ordinance arranges conduct by rule.
Ordain names the act of putting someone in place.
items.exampleCN: ordain 指把某人放到位置上的行为。

items.example: An orderly ward keeps everything in its row.
items.exampleCN: 整齐的病房让一切各在其位。

items.example: A suborder narrows the row of families.

definition_zh: 邀请；请柬；招致
definition_en: a spoken or written request to come somewhere or take part in something
core_image: 一张带香气的卡片被递到手里，上面写着日期和一句话：请来
scene: 邻居敲门，把一张手写卡片递过来，笑着说周末来吃饭。 She accepted the invitation without hesitating.
sceneCN: 这里 invitation 是「邀请」（第 1 个义项：请人前来的请求），句意为她毫不犹豫地接受了邀请。画面里的物件：手写卡片、门框、信封。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「邀请；招致」
由 invite 加 -ing 构成，义为「诱人的」
由 invitation 加 -al 构成，义为「邀请赛的」
加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不请自来的」

senses.title: A request to come
senses.definition: a request asking someone politely to come to a place or event
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地请某人前来某地或参加某活动的请求
senses.example: We got an invitation to their wedding in the post.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在邮件里收到了他们婚礼的邀请。
senses.why: Latin invitare meant to ask someone in, and the noun names the asking.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invitare 意为请人进来，名词指这次邀请。

senses.title: The card itself
senses.definition: the written or printed card that carries such a request
senses.definitionCN: 承载这种请求的书面或印刷卡片
senses.example: The invitation is on the fridge door.
senses.exampleCN: 那张请柬贴在冰箱门上。
senses.why: The paper takes the name of the message it carries.
senses.whyCN: 那张纸随它所承载的话语得了同一个名字。

senses.title: An open opportunity
senses.definition: a chance offered to someone to do or say something
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人做事或说话的机会
senses.example: The pause was an invitation to ask questions.
senses.exampleCN: 那阵停顿等于请人提问。
senses.why: Anything that says come in counts, even silence.
senses.whyCN: 凡是表达「请进」的都算，连沉默也算。

senses.title: Something that attracts harm
senses.definition: a situation or act that seems to encourage something bad
senses.definitionCN: 似乎会招来坏事的行为或状况
senses.example: Leaving the gate open was an invitation to thieves.
senses.exampleCN: 把大门敞着等于招贼。
senses.why: Here the inviting picture turns against the host.
senses.whyCN: 在这里，「邀请」的画面反过来指向主人自己。

intro.en: Invitation comes from Latin invitare, to ask someone in or to treat them as a guest.
intro.cn: invitation 来自拉丁语 invitare，意为请人进来或把对方当客人。

items.en: Invitare meant to invite or to entertain a guest.
items.cn: invitare 意为邀请或款待客人。

items.en: The noun invitatio named the welcoming itself.
items.cn: 名词 invitatio 指这番欢迎。

items.en: French invitation carried the social sense to English.
items.cn: 法语 invitation 把这个社交义带入英语。

items.en: Printed cards made the invitation a thing you keep.
items.cn: 印刷卡片使邀请成为可留存的实物。

items.en: The word also took the darker sense of courting trouble.
items.cn: 这个词也沾上「招来麻烦」的阴暗义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the invit- stem; the near-meaning group holds other social words.
note.cn: 形近组共用 invit- 词干；近义组收其他社交用词。

entries.definition: The verb of asking someone to come.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「邀请」。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning attractive or tempting.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「诱人的」。

entries.definition: The person who is invited.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「受邀者」，与 invitation 拼写相近。

entries.definition: Something presented for acceptance or refusal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「提议」，可接受也可拒绝。

entries.definition: The act of asking for something politely.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「请求」，不一定含欢迎。

entries.definition: An official order to appear.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「传唤」，带有强制。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of a card handed over at the door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「在门口递出一张卡片」的画面。

normal.en: Invite is the verb; invitation is the paper or the words.
normal.cn: invite 是动词，invitation 是那张纸或那番话。

normal.en: Accept, decline, and by invitation only are its three standard partners.
normal.cn: accept、decline、by invitation only 是它的三个固定搭档。

normal.en: An open invitation welcomes you at any time.
normal.cn: an open invitation 是随时欢迎你的邀请。

normal.en: An invitation to trouble is no welcome at all.
normal.cn: an invitation to trouble 根本不是欢迎。

normal.en: Inviting looks inviting, but the noun is about being asked.
normal.cn: inviting 形似 invitation，但名词讲的是被请。

abstract.en: An invitation is a door held open by someone else.
abstract.cn: 邀请是别人替你撑住的门。

abstract.en: To decline an invitation is to close it gently.
abstract.cn: 谢绝邀请是把那扇门轻轻合上。

abstract.en: Some doors invite you in and let the cold follow.
abstract.cn: 有些门请你进去，也把寒冷放了进来。

examples.en: He sent invitations to everyone in the class.
examples.cn: 他给班上每个人都发了请柬。

examples.en: The invitation arrived only two days before the dinner.
examples.cn: 请柬在晚宴前两天才到。

examples.en: Leaving the books outside was an invitation to rain.
examples.cn: 把书搁在门外，等于请雨来浇。

dict_mnemonic.text: invite（邀请）+ ation（名词）——请你来的那句话

root: 拉丁语 invitare「邀请、款待」→ invitatio「邀请」→ 古法语 → 英语 invitation。同族有 invite、inviting、uninvited。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the request, the card that carries it, an offered chance, and something that attracts harm.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：邀请的请求、承载它的卡片、给出的机会，以及招来坏事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a card handed across a threshold by a smiling neighbour.
core.cn: 核心意象：邻居笑着隔着门槛递来一张卡片。

branches.en: THE WEDDING: a request to come and share a day.
branches.cn: 婚礼这条线：请你来共度一天。

branches.en: THE CARD: the printed object on the fridge.
branches.cn: 卡片这条线：贴在冰箱门上的实物。

branches.en: THE PAUSE: a silence that asks a question.
branches.cn: 停顿这条线：请求你发问的沉默。

branches.en: THE OPEN GATE: an invitation nobody meant to give.
branches.cn: 敞开的大门这条线：并非有意发出的邀请。

branches.en: THE LINK: both make room for someone else to act.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都给别人的行动让出位置。

intro.en: Invitation is the Latin noun on invitare, with the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: invitation 是建立在 invitare 上的拉丁语名词，带词尾 -ation。

latinIntro.en: Latin invitare and invitatio are recorded forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 invitare 与 invitatio 均为记载形式。

items.example: The stem is debated by etymologists.
items.exampleCN: 词源学者对这个词干有争论。

items.example: The verb is the direct source.
The noun adds the abstract ending.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词加了抽象词尾。

definition_zh: 跑步者；赛跑者；走私者

core_image: 一双不停向前迈步的腿
scene: 这名跑者在最后一圈超过了所有人。 The runner passed everyone on the final lap.

senses.title: Person who runs
senses.definition: a person who runs
senses.definitionCN: 跑步的人
senses.example: A runner passed us on the hill.

senses.title: Race competitor
senses.definition: a person taking part in a race

senses.why: Carrying things quickly becomes smuggling.

items.en: Rinnan means to flow or run.

items.en: Runnen covers people and water.

items.en: -Er forms the person who runs.

items.en: Runner also names a race competitor.
items.cn: runner 也指赛跑选手。

items.en: Runner extends to illegal couriers.
items.cn: runner 扩展到非法运送者。

note.en: A runner runs; a ruler measures or governs.
note.cn: runner 是跑步的人，ruler 则是尺子或统治者。

entries.definition: a small stream
entries.definitionCN: 小溪

entries.definition: a large drinking glass
entries.definitionCN: 大玻璃杯

entries.definition: a measuring stick
entries.definitionCN: 尺子

entries.definition: someone who runs slowly for exercise
entries.definitionCN: 慢跑者

entries.definition: someone who competes in races
entries.definitionCN: 赛车手；参赛者

entries.definition: someone who carries messages or goods

normalIntro.en: A runner is a person whose job or sport is running.
normalIntro.cn: runner 是以跑步为运动或职业的人。

normal.en: The runner trained for the city race.
normal.cn: 这名跑者为城市赛跑训练。

normal.en: A tired runner stopped at the water station.
normal.cn: 一名疲惫的跑者在补水站停下。

normal.en: She is the fastest runner in her class.
normal.cn: 她是班上跑得最快的人。

normal.en: The runner-up received a silver medal.
normal.cn: 亚军获得了一枚银牌。

normal.en: The police caught the runner at the port.
normal.cn: 警方在港口抓住了那名走私者。

abstract.en: Picture legs moving in a steady rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象双腿以稳定节奏迈动。

abstract.en: Imagine a number on a runner's chest.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者胸前别着号码布。

abstract.en: Think of a parcel passed quickly in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包裹在暗处被快速传递。

examples.en: The runner broke the record by two seconds.
examples.cn: 这名赛跑者以两秒之差打破了纪录。

examples.en: A runner delivered the message before dawn.
examples.cn: 一名信使在黎明前送出了消息。

examples.en: Runners gathered at the start line.
examples.cn: 跑者们聚集在起跑线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「runner」是 run（跑）加 -er：不停跑动的人，就是「跑步者、赛跑者」。

root: 由 run（跑）加施事后缀 -er 构成，run 源自古英语 rinnan（流动、奔跑）。

sensesIntro.en: Runner means a person who runs, a race competitor, or someone who carries goods illegally.
sensesIntro.cn: runner 意为跑步的人、赛跑选手，或非法运送货物的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person in constant forward motion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个持续向前奔跑的人。

branches.en: The base sense is a person who runs.
branches.cn: 基础义是跑步的人。

branches.en: Running becomes an organized race.
branches.cn: 跑步变成有组织的比赛。

branches.en: Fast carrying becomes smuggling.

branches.en: Every racer is first a runner.
