branches.en: Race and illegal delivery both involve speed.
branches.cn: 赛跑与非法运送都强调速度。

intro.en: Runner is run plus the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: runner 是 run 加施事后缀 -er。

latinIntro.en: Runner has no Latin root; run is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: runner 没有拉丁词根，run 属于日耳曼语族。

definition_zh: 组织；筹备；整理；编成团体；使有条理
definition_en: to plan and arrange an activity, to put things into order, to form people into a group or union, or to give separate parts a clear structure
core_image: 散落的零件被一双手按大小排好，一颗颗拧紧，装成一台能转动的机器
scene: 毕业典礼前一天的礼堂里，长桌上堆着没拆的纸箱，几个人来回比对清单，把椅子一排排摆好。 They spent the afternoon organizing the chairs for the ceremony.
sceneCN: 这里的 organizing 是「组织、筹备」（第 1 个义项：筹划并安排一项活动）；句意为他们花了一下午为典礼摆放椅子。图中可辨识物件：纸箱、清单、成排的椅子。

pos.zh: 组织；筹备；整理；编成团体；使有条理

derivatives.zh: 由 organize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「组织；机构」
由 organize 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「组织者」
由 organization 加 -al 构成，义为「组织上的；机构的」

senses.title: To plan and arrange an activity or event
senses.definition: to make all the preparations needed for an activity or event, deciding who does what and when
senses.definitionCN: 为一项活动或事件做好全部准备，把谁做什么、何时做都安排妥当
senses.example: They spent the afternoon organizing the chairs for the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他们花了一下午为典礼摆放椅子。
senses.why: The Greek source organon meant a tool, and the verb came to mean fitting parts together so that a whole can work, which is exactly what planning an event does.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头 organon 意为工具，这个动词后来指把各部分装配合用，使整体能够运转，而筹备一场活动做的正是这件事。

senses.title: To put things into a clear order
senses.definition: to arrange objects, papers or data so that they are easy to find and use
senses.definitionCN: 把物品、文件或资料排放妥当，使人容易查找和使用
senses.example: She organized her notes into three folders before the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前她把笔记整理进三个文件夹。
senses.why: If a tool is a set of parts that fit, then a drawer or a folder can also be made to fit, so the same verb moves from machines to shelves and files.
senses.whyCN: 既然工具是一组彼此契合的部件，抽屉和文件夹也能被安排得彼此契合，于是同一个动词从机器走到了货架和文件。

senses.title: To form people into a group or union
senses.definition: to bring people together into a body with a shared purpose, such as a union or a team
senses.definitionCN: 把人们聚集起来，组成一个有共同目标的团体，如工会或队伍
senses.example: The workers organized a union in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们在春天组织成立了一个工会。
senses.why: People, like parts, can be brought into a working arrangement, and when they act as one body the verb names the forming of that body.
senses.whyCN: 人和零件一样可以被装进一个能运转的安排里，当他们作为一个整体行动时，这个动词指的就是这个整体的形成。

senses.title: To arrange parts into a coherent whole
senses.definition: to give separate pieces of something, such as an essay or a plan, a logical and clear structure
senses.definitionCN: 给文章、方案等分散的部分安排出合乎逻辑而清晰的结构
senses.example: The report was poorly organized, so the main point was hard to find.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告编排得很乱，主旨很难找到。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the root is an instrument whose parts work together, and writing is organized when each paragraph has a job in the whole.
senses.whyCN: 这个词根最老的意思是各部件协同工作的器具，而文章之所以「有条理」，正是因为每段都在整体里担着一份职责。

intro.en: Organize came through medieval Latin from the Greek word for a tool; the tool image is the reason the verb can mean arranging parts, forming groups and giving a text a structure.
intro.cn: organize 经中世纪拉丁语上溯到希腊语中表示「工具」的词；正因为有这件工具的画面，这个动词才能表示装配部件、组成团体与安排文章结构。

items.en: Organon meant a tool or instrument, especially one made of parts that work together for a task.
items.cn: organon 意为工具、器具，尤指由若干协同工作的部件构成、用于某项任务的器具。

items.en: Latin took the word as organum, an instrument or a bodily organ, and also used it for a musical instrument.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该词作 organum，指器具或身体器官，也用来指乐器。

items.en: Medieval Latin formed organizare, to organize or to give something its organs and parts, often used of the body and of a body of people.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出 organizare，意为组织、赋予某物器官与部件，常用于身体，也用于一群人构成的团体。

items.en: French took the verb as organiser, meaning to arrange or to set up, and English borrowed it in the same practical sense.
items.cn: 法语把该动词作 organiser，意为安排、设立，英语借入时也带着同样实用的意味。

items.en: Modern English keeps organize for events, for shelves and files, for unions and teams, and for the structure of writing or plans.
items.cn: 现代英语让 organize 兼指活动筹备、货架与文件的整理、工会与队伍的组织，以及文章或方案的结构安排。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the Greek and Latin stem for tool and organ; the near-meaning group collects verbs for putting things into order.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在希腊语与拉丁语「工具、器官」词干上的词；近义组收表示「把事物安排有序」的动词。

entries.definition: A part of the body with a special job, or a large musical instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 身体中担负特定功能的部位，或大型乐器。

entries.definition: Relating to living things, or grown without artificial chemicals.
entries.definitionCN: 与生物有关的，或不用人工化学物质种植的。

entries.definition: The act of arranging, or a group that has been arranged.
entries.definitionCN: 安排的行为，或被组织起来的团体。

entries.definition: A person who plans and arranges an event.
entries.definitionCN: 筹划并安排活动的人。

entries.definition: To put things in a particular order or position.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物按某种次序或位置放好。

entries.definition: To make different parts work together smoothly.
entries.definitionCN: 使不同部分顺畅地配合运作。

entries.definition: To separate things into groups by type.
entries.definitionCN: 按种类把事物分成组。

entries.definition: To put things into named categories.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物归入有名目的类别。

normalIntro.en: Organize rests on the Greek word for a tool, so its hooks keep the picture of separate parts being fitted into something that works.
normalIntro.cn: organize 建立在希腊语表示「工具」的词上，所以记忆钩子始终保留「分散的部件被装成一件能用的东西」的画面。

normal.en: The Greek word organon is a tool, and an organ in the body is a tool of that organ's own kind, which is why the family keeps the sense of parts that work.
normal.cn: 希腊语 organon 是工具，而身体里的器官正是各自那一类的工具，所以这一族词始终带着「部件在起作用」的意味。

normal.en: Organize ends in -ize, the verb ending that means to make or to put into a state, so to organize is to make something into an ordered body.
normal.cn: organize 以 -ize 收尾，这个动词词尾表示「使成为某种状态」，所以组织就是把某物变成一个有序的整体。

normal.en: Organization is organize plus -ation, the ending that names an action or its result, so the same stem gives both the act and the body.
normal.cn: organization 是 organize 加 -ation，这个后缀指行为或其结果，所以同一个词干既给出动作，也给出团体。

normal.en: Organize a meeting and organize information share one verb because both put scattered pieces into a workable order.
normal.cn: organize a meeting 与 organize information 共用一个动词，因为两者都把零散的东西排成可用的次序。

normal.en: Note the British spelling with s and the American spelling with z, just as organisation and organization differ.
normal.cn: 留意英式拼写用 s、美式拼写用 z，正如 organisation 与 organization 的差别。

abstract.en: A word that began with a tool reminds us that order is not decoration; it is what makes separate parts able to do something together.
abstract.cn: 一个从工具起步的词提醒人：秩序不是装饰，而是让分散部件能一起做成一件事的条件。

abstract.en: To organize people is to treat them as parts of one body, which is powerful and also a little dangerous.
abstract.cn: 把人组织起来，就是把他们当作一个整体的部件，这既有力量，也带一点危险。

abstract.en: Every tidy shelf and every clear paragraph is the same small victory over scatter.
abstract.cn: 每一个整齐的货架、每一段清晰的文字，都是对「散乱」的同一场小小胜利。

examples.en: They spent the afternoon organizing the chairs for the ceremony.
examples.cn: 他们花了一下午为典礼摆放椅子。

examples.en: She organized her notes into three folders.
examples.cn: 她把笔记整理进三个文件夹。

examples.en: The workers organized a union in the spring.
examples.cn: 工人们在春天组织成立了一个工会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，搁那儿整」——东西都搁在那儿，一件件整好；记住 organize 是整理、组织。

root: 来自中世纪拉丁语 organizare（组织、使成系统），再上溯拉丁语 organum（工具、器官），源头是希腊语 organon（器具）；同族词多与「器官、机构、有机关联的整体」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is parts fitted into a working whole; the senses divide by what is fitted together, an event, a set of objects, a group of people, or the pieces of a text.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是部件被装成一个能运转的整体；义项按被装配的对象分出：一场活动、一堆物品、一群人，或一篇文章的各个部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered parts sorted by size and screwed together into a machine that turns.
core.cn: 核心意象：散落的零件被按大小排好，拧成一台能转动的机器。

branches.en: a hall being made ready for a ceremony
branches.cn: 为典礼布置好的一座礼堂

branches.en: papers and boxes sorted into neat rows
branches.cn: 纸张与箱子被分成整齐的几排

branches.en: workers signing their names to a new union
branches.cn: 工人在新工会名册上签名

branches.en: an essay whose paragraphs finally fall into place
branches.cn: 段落终于各就各位的一篇文章

branches.en: the same verb for an event and a shelf
branches.cn: 同一个动词，既用于活动，也用于货架

intro.en: The word is a Greek tool-noun that became a Latin organ-word, then a medieval verb, and English adds the endings that name the act and the person.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语的「工具」名词，先变成拉丁语的「器官」词，再变成中世纪的动词，英语又加上词尾来指行为与人。

latinIntro.en: Greek organon, Latin organum and medieval Latin organizare are all recorded, so this family has a reliable ancestry even though it crossed three languages.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 organon、拉丁语 organum 与中世纪拉丁语 organizare 均有记录，因此这一族词虽有三次跨语言，世系仍然可靠。

items.meaning: to arrange or form into a whole
the act of organizing, or a body so formed
to make, to put into a state

definition_zh: 完美的；理想的；完全的；使完善；完成时
definition_en: having no fault and being as good as possible; exactly suitable; complete in every way; to make something fully developed
core_image: 一块被反复打磨的木头，棱角全部消失，表面能照出人的影子
scene: 木工房里，老师傅换掉最后一道砂纸，用指腹顺着木纹摸了一遍。 He kept sanding until the surface felt perfect under his fingers.
sceneCN: 这里 perfect 是「完美的、无可挑剔的」（第 1 个义项：质地没有任何缺陷）；句意是他不肯停手，直到指腹摸到的表面毫无瑕疵。

derivatives.zh: 由 perfect 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「完美；完善」
由 perfect 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「完美地；完全地」
由否定前缀 im- 加 perfect 构成，义为「不完美的」
由 perfection 加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「完美主义者」

senses.title: Flawless in quality
senses.definition: so good in every detail that no fault can be found
senses.definitionCN: 每个细节都好到挑不出毛病
senses.example: Her piano playing is almost perfect.
senses.exampleCN: 她的钢琴演奏几乎无可挑剔。
senses.why: Perfectus is the past participle of a verb meaning to finish thoroughly, so the adjective first says finished, then finished so well that nothing at all is missing.
senses.whyCN: perfectus 本是一个意为「彻底做完」的动词的过去分词，所以这个形容词先说「做完了」，再说「做完到一点都不缺」，于是成了无可挑剔。

senses.title: Exactly suitable
senses.definition: the best possible thing for a particular purpose or person
senses.definitionCN: 对某个用途或某个人来说最合适的那一个
senses.example: The little courtyard is perfect for summer evenings.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小院子最适合夏夜。
senses.why: Once a thing is complete, it meets its purpose with nothing left over and nothing short, so the word slides from nothing lacking to nothing mismatched.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西一旦完整，就恰好满足它的用途，既不多余也不欠缺，于是词义从「什么都不缺」滑到「什么都不错配」。

senses.title: Complete, used for emphasis
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean complete, often when someone is surprised or annoyed
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前表示「完全的」，常带惊讶或恼火的语气
senses.example: I felt like a perfect fool.
senses.exampleCN: 我觉得自己十足是个傻瓜。
senses.why: The old sense of thoroughly done survives here as bare emphasis: nothing is added to the noun except the claim that it is complete all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 「彻底做完」这个旧义在这里变成纯粹的强调：名词之外没有增加任何内容，只多了一句「从头到尾都够彻底」。

senses.title: To make something fully developed
senses.definition: to improve something through repeated work until it reaches its best possible form
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复打磨把某物改进到它能达到的最好状态
senses.example: She perfected her accent by listening to recordings.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠听录音把自己的口音打磨得很地道。
senses.why: The verb keeps the Latin prefix per-, meaning through, and so exposes the work hidden inside the adjective: carrying a thing through to the end.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了拉丁语前缀 per-（穿过、彻底），因此把形容词里藏着的过程露了出来：把一件事一直做到头。

senses.title: The tense of completed action
senses.definition: the verb form that presents an action as finished rather than still going on
senses.definitionCN: 把动作呈现为已经完成、而不是仍在进行的动词形式
senses.example: In the perfect tense, the sentence uses have plus a past participle.
senses.exampleCN: 在完成时里，句子用 have 加过去分词。
senses.why: Grammarians took perfectus in its literal sense of finished and applied it to a verb form whose whole job is to say that an action is done.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家取 perfectus 字面上的「已完成」，把它安在一种专门表示动作已经做完的动词形式上。

intro.en: Perfect is built from two Latin pieces, a prefix meaning through and a verb meaning to make, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: perfect 由两个拉丁成分拼成，一个意为「彻底」的前缀，一个意为「做」的动词，并经法语进入英语。

items.en: The verb perficere joined per-, through, to facere, to do or make: to carry something through to the end.
items.cn: 动词 perficere 由表「穿过、彻底」的 per- 与 facere（做、造）组合，意为把一件事做到底。

items.en: Its past participle perfectus meant thoroughly made or finished, and only later gathered the sense of excellent quality.
items.cn: 它的过去分词 perfectus 意为「彻底做成的、完成的」，后来才带上称赞质量的意思。

items.en: Old French inherited the word as parfait, keeping both the sense of finished and the sense of excellent.
items.cn: 古法语继承为 parfait，把「完成」与「出色」两层意思一并保留。

items.en: Middle English took the adjective from French, and later formed a verb from the same stem, so one spelling now does two jobs.
items.cn: 中古英语从法语借入形容词，后来又用同一词干造出动词，于是一个拼写承担两种词性。

items.en: Modern English keeps the two apart only by stress: the adjective is stressed first, the verb last, and the spelling never shows it.
items.cn: 现代英语只靠重音区分二者：形容词前重，动词后重，而拼写完全看不出来。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the word family built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group collects adjectives that describe something without fault.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词族；近义组收表示「没有缺陷」的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being perfect, or the act of making something perfect.
entries.definitionCN: 完美的状态，或使某物完善的行为。

entries.definition: Having faults or missing parts, the direct opposite of the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 有缺陷或缺部分的，正好是形容词的反面。

entries.definition: The adverb made from perfect, meaning in a flawless or complete way.
entries.definitionCN: 由 perfect 构成的副词，意为完美地或完全地。

entries.definition: A person who is not satisfied with anything below a perfect standard.
entries.definitionCN: 对达不到完美标准的东西就不满意的人。

entries.definition: Without any fault, crack or weakness at all.
entries.definitionCN: 完全没有缺点、裂痕或弱点的。

entries.definition: The best that can be imagined for a purpose, rather than one that exists.
entries.definitionCN: 对某个用途而言能想象到的最好状态，而非已经存在的。

entries.definition: Showing no mistake, used especially of performance and technique.
entries.definitionCN: 没有失误的，尤用于表演与技术。

entries.definition: Complete in skill, carried to the highest level by long practice.
entries.definitionCN: 技艺炉火纯青的，经过长期练习达到最高水平。

normalIntro.en: The word divides into a prefix of thoroughness and a Latin verb of making, and its grammar sense comes from the same picture of a finished job.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词可拆成表「彻底」的前缀与表「做」的拉丁动词，它的语法义项也来自「活干完了」这个同一幅画面。

normal.en: Per- in perficere means through, and facere means make, so perfect starts life as made through and through.
normal.cn: perficere 里的 per- 意为穿过，facere 意为做，所以 perfect 的起点是「里外都做透」。

normal.en: The element -fect is a worn form of facere, and the same piece sits in defect, effect and infect, all about doing or making.
normal.cn: -fect 是 facere 磨损后的样子，同一成分也出现在 defect、effect、infect 里，都与做、造成有关。

normal.en: The adjective and the verb differ only in stress: the first syllable carries the describing sense, the second the acting one.
normal.cn: 形容词与动词只差重音：重音在前是「完美的」，在后是「使完美」。

normal.en: Practice makes perfect uses the adjective in its oldest sense, finished by repeated work rather than lucky from the start.
normal.cn: practice makes perfect 用的是形容词最老的意思：靠反复练习做出来的完成，而不是天生的好运。

normal.en: Add -ion and you get perfection, the state of having nothing left to improve.
normal.cn: 加上 -ion 就得到 perfection，即再也没有可改进之处的状态。

abstract.en: A surface polished until no scratch catches the light is the whole idea of the adjective in one glance.
abstract.cn: 一块磨到任何划痕都不反光的表面，一眼就能说明这个形容词的全部意思。

abstract.en: The verb is the hand still moving over that surface, which is why the same letters hold both the result and the work.
abstract.cn: 动词是仍在那块表面上移动的手，所以同样的字母既装得下结果，也装得下过程。

abstract.en: Grammar borrowed the word because a finished action and a flawless object share one picture: nothing left over, nothing missing.
abstract.cn: 语法借用了这个词，因为「做完的动作」与「无瑕的物件」共用一幅画面：没有多余，也没有欠缺。

examples.en: Her piano playing is almost perfect.
examples.cn: 她的钢琴演奏几乎无可挑剔。

examples.en: She perfected her accent by listening to recordings.
examples.cn: 她靠听录音把自己的口音打磨得很地道。

examples.en: The old table is still in perfect condition.
examples.cn: 这张旧桌子依然完好无损。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「颇费刻」——颇费功夫去雕刻，才刻得出完美的作品。

root: 拉丁语 per-（彻底）+ facere（做、造）→ perficere（做完）→ perfectus（完成的、完美的）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a job done all the way through; from that grow the ideas of flawlessness, exact fit, plain emphasis, the act of improving, and the grammar of finished action.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「一件事被做透」；无可挑剔、恰好合适、纯粹强调、使之完善以及完成时，都从这里长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a piece of wood sanded until no edge is left and the surface mirrors a face.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被反复打磨的木头，棱角全部消失，表面能照出人的影子。

branches.en: a mirror surface with no scratch in it
branches.cn: 没有一道划痕的镜面

branches.en: a key that turns without the least resistance
branches.cn: 毫不费力就转开的钥匙

branches.en: a stranger who knows nobody in the room
branches.cn: 屋里谁也不认识的陌生人

branches.en: a hand going back over the same board once more
branches.cn: 在同一块板上又走一遍的手

branches.en: a sentence that reports a thing as already done
branches.cn: 把事说成已经做完的句子

intro.en: A Latin prefix of thoroughness and a Latin verb of making hold the whole family together, from the adjective to the grammar term.
intro.cn: 一个表「彻底」的拉丁前缀与一个表「做」的拉丁动词撑起整族词，从形容词一直到语法术语。

latinIntro.en: Perficere, perfectus and facere are all recorded Latin forms; the only doubtful point is how early the praising sense appeared in French.
latinIntro.cn: perficere、perfectus、facere 都是有记载的拉丁形式；唯一存疑之处是「称赞」这层意思在法语里出现得多早。

definition_zh: 打扰；使烦恼；费心；麻烦（名词）
definition_en: to annoy or worry someone, to make an effort, or a troublesome thing
core_image: 正在专心写字时，一只手在你肩上拍了一下
scene: 孩子正专心写作业，弟弟在门口大声喊他，他只好放下笔。 The noise bothered him while he was studying.
sceneCN: 这里 bother 是「打扰；使烦恼」（第 1 个义项：打断别人并让其不快）；句意为学习时那声音打扰了他。

pos.zh: 名词：麻烦；令人烦恼的事

derivatives.zh: 由 bother 加 -some 构成，义为「令人烦恼的；讨厌的」
由 un- 与 bothered 构成，义为「不受打扰的；不在意的」
由 bother 加 -ation 构成，义为「麻烦；恼人的事」，也用作感叹

senses.title: To interrupt and disturb
senses.definition: to interrupt someone who is busy, or to disturb them with noise and questions
senses.definitionCN: 打断正在忙的人，或用噪音和问话干扰他
senses.example: Sorry to bother you at this hour.
senses.exampleCN: 抱歉在这个时间打扰你。
senses.why: Bother first meant to deafen or buzz in the ear, so interrupting someone grew from that noisy picture.
senses.whyCN: bother 最初有「震耳、在耳边嗡嗡响」的意思，所以「打扰」是从那幅吵闹的画面长出来的。

senses.title: To worry or upset
senses.definition: to make someone feel annoyed, worried or uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到恼火、担心或不舒服
senses.example: The noise bothered the neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 那噪音让邻居们很烦。
senses.why: The same disturbance can land inside a person as worry, so the verb also means to upset someone.
senses.whyCN: 同样的干扰也可以落在人心里变成担忧，所以这个动词也指使人心烦。

senses.title: To take the trouble
senses.definition: to make an effort to do something, usually used in questions and negatives
senses.definitionCN: 花力气去做某事，常用于疑问句和否定句
senses.example: Don't bother waiting for me.
senses.exampleCN: 不用费心等我了。
senses.why: If a task is a bother, then bothering to do it means accepting the trouble it costs.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件事本身就是麻烦，那么 bothering to do it 就是接受它为这事付出的麻烦。

senses.title: A troublesome thing
senses.definition: a person or thing that causes trouble or extra effort
senses.definitionCN: 带来麻烦或额外费力的人或事
senses.example: Filling in these forms is a real bother.
senses.exampleCN: 填这些表格真是件麻烦事。
senses.why: The verb became a noun, so the trouble itself is simply called a bother.
senses.whyCN: 动词变成名词，于是麻烦本身就直接被叫作 a bother。

intro.en: Bother is a fairly young word, first recorded in the eighteenth century, and its deeper origin is not certain.
intro.cn: bother 是相当年轻的词，最早记录于十八世纪，更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Bother appears in English writing in the eighteenth century, first as a word for noisy disturbance.
items.cn: bother 在十八世纪的英语文献中出现，最初指吵闹的干扰。

items.en: Some scholars connect it with a dialect word meaning to buzz or deafen, but the link is not proved.
items.cn: 有学者把它与一个表示嗡嗡响或震耳的方言词联系起来，但这条线并未得到证实。

items.en: No old Germanic or Latin root can be securely traced, so the deeper history stays uncertain.
items.cn: 无法可靠追溯到古老的日耳曼语或拉丁语词根，所以更早的历史仍不确定。

items.en: From disturbance the verb spread to worry, to effort and finally to the noun meaning trouble.
items.cn: 从「干扰」出发，这个动词扩展到担心、费力，最后又产生名词「麻烦」。

items.en: Today bother covers interruption, worry, effort and a troublesome task.
items.cn: 今天 bother 覆盖打断、担心、费力与恼人的事情。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in shape; the near-meaning group collects words about disturbing and annoying.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写接近的词；近义组收与打扰、烦恼有关的词。

entries.definition: A boy or man with the same parents as you.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「兄弟」，拼写与 bother 相近。

entries.definition: A female parent.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「母亲」，拼写与 bother 相近。

entries.definition: A container for liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「瓶子」，读音与 bother 接近。

entries.definition: To interrupt someone or break their quiet.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「打扰；扰乱」，对应 bother 的打扰义。

entries.definition: To make someone slightly angry.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使恼火」，对应 bother 的烦恼义。

entries.definition: A problem or something that causes extra effort.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「麻烦」，对应 bother 的名词义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Bother is first recorded in the eighteenth century, and its deeper root is uncertain.
normal.cn: bother 最早记录于十八世纪，更早的词根并不确定。

normal.en: It began with noisy disturbance, which is why it suits interruptions so well.
normal.cn: 它从吵闹的干扰开始，所以特别适合表示「打断」。

normal.en: If a task is a bother, bothering to do it means accepting the trouble.
normal.cn: 如果一件事本身就是麻烦，bothering to do it 就是接受这份麻烦。

normal.en: It commonly pairs with sorry, don't, about and someone.
normal.cn: 它常与 sorry、don't、about、someone 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-o-t-h-e-r; the th is voiced, as in this.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-o-t-h-e-r，th 读作浊音，就像 this 里的音。

abstract.en: See a hand tap your shoulder while you are writing: that tap is bother.
abstract.cn: 想象你正在写字时，一只手在你肩上拍了一下：那一拍就是 bother。

abstract.en: Let the tap become a buzzing sound that stays in the ear, and the word deepens.
abstract.cn: 让那一拍变成耳边挥之不去的嗡嗡声，这个词的意思就加深了。

abstract.en: Say the word and let the tapping hand bring the sense back.
abstract.cn: 先读这个词，再让那只拍肩的手把意思带回来。

examples.en: Sorry to bother you at this hour.
examples.cn: 抱歉在这个时间打扰你。

examples.en: The noise bothered the neighbours.
examples.cn: 那噪音让邻居们很烦。

examples.en: Don't bother waiting for me.
examples.cn: 不用费心等我了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「波泽」——写字时肩上被拍了一下：打扰

root: bother 是十八世纪才出现在英语中的年轻词，最初指吵闹的干扰；有学者把它与表示嗡嗡响或震耳的方言词联系起来，但这条线未获证实，更早的词根无法可靠追溯。由「干扰」出发，它扩展到担心、费力，最后又产生名词「麻烦」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses of bother rest on one picture: something noisy or sudden landing on a person who is busy.
sensesIntro.cn: bother 的四个义项都立在同一个画面上：某种吵闹或突然的东西，落在正忙的人身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tapping your shoulder while you write
core.cn: 核心意象：你写字时肩上被拍了一下

branches.en: THE INTERRUPTION: disturbing a busy person is the first sense.
branches.cn: 打断线：干扰一个正在忙的人，是第一个义项。

branches.en: THE WORRY: the same disturbance lands inside as upset.
branches.cn: 担心线：同样的干扰落在心里变成不快。

branches.en: THE EFFORT: accepting a task's trouble is also called bothering.
branches.cn: 费力线：接受一件事的麻烦，也叫 bothering。

branches.en: THE NUISANCE: the noun names the troublesome thing itself.
branches.cn: 麻烦线：名词指的就是那件恼人的事。

branches.en: THE DISTURBANCE: an outside noise and an inner upset share one image.
branches.cn: 干扰线：外面的噪音与心里的不快共享同一幅画面。

intro.en: Bother is a base verb and noun, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: bother 是基础动词兼名词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vexare and molestare are recorded verbs for troubling someone; they are parallels, not the source of bother.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vexare 与 molestare 是有记录的「使人烦恼」动词，它们是平行词，不是 bother 的来源。

items.example: It is first recorded in the eighteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 它最早记录于十八世纪。

items.example: It forms sorry to bother you.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 sorry to bother you。

items.example: It forms a fuss and a bother.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 a fuss and a bother。

definition_zh: 咸的；含盐的；粗俗的；恼火的
definition_en: containing or tasting of salt; (of language) coarse or earthy; (informal) bitter or resentful
core_image: 舌尖碰到海水时那股明显的咸味
scene: 这汤太咸了，我喝不下去。 This soup is too salty for me to drink.
sceneCN: 这里 salty 是「咸的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这汤太咸了，我喝不下去。

senses.title: Tasting of salt
senses.definition: containing salt or having the taste of salt
senses.definitionCN: 含盐或有盐味的
senses.example: The chips are very salty.
senses.exampleCN: 这些薯片很咸。
senses.why: The basic sense describes the taste of salt.
senses.whyCN: 基础义就是描述盐的味道。

senses.title: Coarse in speech
senses.definition: using language that is rude or earthy
senses.definitionCN: 使用粗鲁或粗鄙的语言
senses.example: He told a salty joke at dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 他在晚餐时讲了个粗俗的笑话。
senses.why: The sharp taste of salt becomes a metaphor for sharp words.
senses.whyCN: 盐的刺激味道被喻为尖锐的言辞。

senses.title: Bitter or annoyed
senses.definition: feeling angry or resentful, especially in informal use
senses.definitionCN: 感到生气或怨恨，尤用于非正式场合
senses.example: She was still salty about losing the game.
senses.exampleCN: 她还在为输掉比赛而恼火。
senses.why: Modern slang extends the sharp taste to a sharp mood.
senses.whyCN: 现代俚语把尖锐的味道引申为尖锐的情绪。

intro.en: Salty is formed from salt with the adjective ending -y.
intro.cn: salty 由 salt 加形容词后缀 -y 构成。

items.en: Sealtig already describes a salty taste.
items.cn: 古英语 sealtig 已表示咸味。

items.en: The form shortens toward salty.
items.cn: 中古英语时期形式缩短为 salty。

items.en: Salty describes seawater and preserved food.
items.cn: 早期现代英语中 salty 描述海水与腌制品。

items.en: The word gains a sense of coarse speech.
items.cn: 十九世纪增添「言语粗俗」之义。

items.en: Salty comes to mean annoyed or resentful.
items.cn: 现代俚语中 salty 表示恼火或怨愤。

note.en: Salty means full of salt; salt is the substance itself.
note.cn: salty 是「咸的」，salt 则是盐本身。

entries.definition: the white seasoning itself
entries.definitionCN: 盐

entries.definition: to greet with respect
entries.definitionCN: 致敬；行礼

entries.definition: hot and humid
entries.definitionCN: 闷热的

entries.definition: full of salt water
entries.definitionCN: 咸的；多盐水的

entries.definition: salty or spicy rather than sweet
entries.definitionCN: 咸香的；开胃的

entries.definition: flavoured with salt or spices
entries.definitionCN: 调过味的

normalIntro.en: Salty adds -y to salt to describe the taste.
normalIntro.cn: salty 在 salt 后加 -y，用来描述味道。

normal.en: The sea air felt salty on my lips.
normal.cn: 海风让我嘴唇感到咸咸的。

normal.en: I prefer salty snacks to sweet ones.
normal.cn: 比起甜零食，我更喜欢咸零食。

normal.en: The soup became too salty after I added sauce.
normal.cn: 我加了酱之后汤变得太咸了。

normal.en: His salty jokes upset some guests.
normal.cn: 他粗俗的笑话让一些客人不快。

normal.en: He is still salty about the result.
normal.cn: 他对结果仍然耿耿于怀。

abstract.en: Picture waves leaving a white ring on your skin.
abstract.cn: 想象海浪在皮肤上留下一圈白痕。

abstract.en: Imagine words as sharp grains of salt.
abstract.cn: 把尖锐的言辞想成刺人的盐粒。

abstract.en: Think of a face pulled tight by an old grudge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张因旧怨而绷紧的脸。

examples.en: The popcorn was buttery and salty.
examples.cn: 这爆米花又香又咸。

examples.en: Salty water is not safe to drink.
examples.cn: 咸水不能安全饮用。

examples.en: He gets salty whenever his team loses.
examples.cn: 他的球队一输球他就恼火。

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · 后缀派生
dict_mnemonic.text: salt（盐）+ -y（形容词后缀）= salty（咸的），词尾变化规则与 rain → rainy 相同。

root: salty 由 salt（盐）加形容词后缀 -y 构成，与古英语 sealtig 一脉相承。

sensesIntro.en: Salty describes a salt taste, coarse speech, or an annoyed mood.
sensesIntro.cn: salty 描述咸味、粗俗言语或恼火的情绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sharp taste of salt on the tongue.
core.cn: 核心意象：舌尖上尖锐的盐味。

branches.en: The base sense is the taste of salt.
branches.cn: 基础义是盐的味道。

branches.en: Sharp taste becomes a metaphor for sharp words.
branches.cn: 尖锐的味道成为尖锐言辞的隐喻。

branches.en: Slang turns the taste into a bitter mood.
branches.cn: 俚语把味道转成怨愤的情绪。

branches.en: Both senses keep the idea of something sharp.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留「尖锐」的意味。

branches.en: Coarse words and angry feelings often travel together.
branches.cn: 粗话与怒气常常相伴出现。

intro.en: The suffix -y turns the noun salt into the adjective salty.
intro.cn: 后缀 -y 把名词 salt 变成形容词 salty。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base sal also produced saline and salinity in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 sal 在英语中还产生了 saline 与 salinity。

items.example: The broth is a little salty.
This sauce is saltier than that one.
It is the saltiest soup on the menu.
The saltiness comes from the cheese.
The dish tastes saltily of the sea.
items.exampleCN: 这道菜带着海水的咸味。

items.example: They serve an unsalty version for children.
items.exampleCN: 他们为孩子提供不咸的版本。

items.example: Saltwater taffy is a seaside treat.
items.exampleCN: 咸水太妃糖是一种海滨小吃。

items.example: The nurse used a saline drip.
items.exampleCN: 护士用了生理盐水点滴。

items.meaning: the amount of salt in water
items.exampleCN: 高盐度会伤害许多植物。

latinEntries.example: Sal is the root of saline.
latinEntries.exampleCN: sal 是 saline 的词根。

definition_zh: 然而；可是；无论如何；不管多么
definition_en: used to introduce a contrast with what was said before, or to say that it makes no difference how much or how
core_image: 话说到一半，手臂横着一挡：先停一下，再说「但是」
scene: 天气预报说有雨，他仍背起书包出了门。 The sky was dark; however, we still went out to play.
sceneCN: 这里 however 是副词「然而；可是」（第 1 个义项：引出转折）；天色很暗，但我们还是出门玩了。

pos.zh: 不管用什么方式；无论多么

collocations.zh: 随你怎么弄；以你喜欢的任何方式

senses.title: Introducing a contrast
senses.definition: used to join a sentence that contrasts with the one before it
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出与前文意思相反的句子
senses.example: The plan sounded easy. However, it took two weeks to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划听起来容易。然而，实际花了两周才完成。
senses.why: The core use is a small stop sign between two opposite statements.
senses.whyCN: 核心用法是立在两个相反说法之间的小小停车牌。

senses.title: No matter how much or how
senses.definition: used to say that degree or manner makes no difference to the result
senses.definitionCN: 表示程度或方式都不影响结果
senses.example: However hard he tried, the door would not open.
senses.exampleCN: 无论他多用力推，门都打不开。
senses.why: The question word how keeps its old job: however repeats the question and cancels it.
senses.whyCN: 疑问词 how 保留原职：however 把疑问重复一遍又把它取消。

senses.title: In whatever way one chooses
senses.definition: in whatever manner someone chooses or manages
senses.definitionCN: 以某人选择的任何方式
senses.example: Do it however you like; the result is yours.
senses.exampleCN: 随你怎么做，结果由你负责。
senses.why: All the possible ways are swept together and given away as a free choice.
senses.whyCN: 所有可能的方式被一揽子收起，交还成一份自由选择。

intro.en: However is simply how plus ever, an English compound that grew in the Middle English period.
intro.cn: however 就是 how 加 ever，是中古英语时期长出的英语复合词。

items.en: Old English hu asked the manner; ever has the sense of at any time.
items.cn: 古英语 hu 问方式；ever 义为「在任何时候」。

items.en: In Middle English, how ever was first two words, then joined into however.
items.cn: 中古英语中 how ever 起初分写，后来合并成 however。

items.en: The contrast use developed beside the no-matter use in the same period.
items.cn: 同一时期，「转折」用法与「无论」用法并行发展。

items.en: Modern English family grew parallel forms: whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever.
items.cn: 现代英语长出平行家族：whatever、whenever、wherever、whoever。

items.en: Both halves are Germanic native words, like how itself.
items.cn: 两半都是日耳曼本族词，与 how 一脉相承。

note.en: Group one keeps the ever compounds; group two keeps contrast words.
note.cn: 第一组是 -ever 复合词；第二组是表示转折的近义词。

entries.definition: no matter what
entries.definitionCN: 同构词，义为「无论什么」

entries.definition: no matter when; at any time
entries.definitionCN: 同构词，义为「无论何时」

entries.definition: no matter who
entries.definitionCN: 同构词，义为「无论是谁」

entries.definition: the shortest contrast word
entries.definitionCN: but，最短的转折词

entries.definition: in spite of that
entries.definitionCN: 尽管如此，较正式

entries.definition: used to add a surprising contrast
entries.definitionCN: yet，引出令人意外的对比

normalIntro.en: Split the word and use the -ever family.
normalIntro.cn: 拆开这个词，用 -ever 家族记它。

normal.en: how + ever = however: the question repeated and cancelled
normal.cn: how + ever＝however：疑问被重复又被取消＝无论如何。

normal.en: however hard, however late: degree does not matter
normal.cn: however hard、however late：程度再大也不影响结果。

normal.en: however, with a comma, means but between sentences
normal.cn: however 后加逗号＝句间的「但是」。

normal.en: whatever, whenever, whoever follow the same pattern
normal.cn: whatever、whenever、whoever 与 it 同构。

normal.en: however you like hands the choice to you
normal.cn: however you like＝选择权交给你＝随你怎么做。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand stopping a sentence in mid-air.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抬起的把句子拦在半空的手——转折的停顿。

abstract.en: Picture rain, storm and wind, yet the little boat sails on regardless.
abstract.cn: 想象风雨交加，小船照样前行——无论如何。

abstract.en: Feel however as a door that opens no matter how you push it.
abstract.cn: 把 however 感受成一扇怎么推都会开的门。

examples.en: He was tired; however, he finished all his homework.
examples.cn: 他很累了，然而他仍然做完了全部作业。

examples.en: However cold it is, the old man swims every morning.
examples.cn: 无论多冷，老人每天早晨都游泳。

examples.en: You may arrange the desks however you like.
examples.cn: 课桌随你怎么摆都行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「好外娃」——好在外面起了个娃（转折小插曲），however 就是「然而」里带的那个意外。

root: however 由本族词 how（怎样）+ ever（任何）复合而成，中古英语由分写合为一词；与 whatever、whenever 等同构，皆属日耳曼成分。

sensesIntro.en: However both blocks a sentence with a contrast and sweeps away every degree and manner.
sensesIntro.cn: however 一手立转折、一手抹平一切程度与方式：既当「然而」，又当「无论多么」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand that stops and then releases
core.cn: 核心意象：先拦住、再放行的抬手

branches.en: the stop sign before a contrast
branches.cn: 转折前的停车牌（义项 01）

branches.en: the degree that changes nothing
branches.cn: 不影响结果的任何程度（义项 02）

branches.en: the choice handed back free
branches.cn: 交还的自由选择（义项 03）

branches.en: contrast and concession share one word
branches.cn: 转折与让步共用一词（义项 01 · 02）

branches.en: nothing and everything both allowed
branches.cn: 什么都不设限，什么都允许（义项 02 · 03）

intro.en: However is built from two native words and heads a whole family of -ever compounds.
intro.cn: however 由两个本族词构成，并带出一整族 -ever 复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin qualitercumque, in whatever way, is the classical counterpart.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 qualitercumque（无论以何方式）是古典对照词。

items.example: However you see it, it is a loss.
items.exampleCN: 无论你怎么看，这都是损失。
ever 起强化疑问词的作用
无论发生什么，都要冷静。
你什么时候有空就什么时候来。

items.example: It rained; nevertheless we marched on.
items.exampleCN: 天下着雨，尽管如此我们仍继续前进。

items.meaningCN: 无论以何方式（拉丁对照词）
items.exampleCN: 由 qualiter 与 cumque 构成。

definition_zh: 包括；包含；把……算入
definition_en: to have something as a part of a whole, or to make something part of a group
core_image: 一个圈把东西圈进去：圈里的都算数
scene: 菜单打印好了，米饭和汤已经写进套餐里。 The set meal includes soup and rice.
sceneCN: 这里 include 是「包括」（第 1 个义项：作为整体的一部分）；句意：套餐包含汤和米饭。

derivatives.zh: include 加过去分词后缀，义为「包含在内的」
include 的介词用法，义为「包括」
include 加名词后缀，义为「包含；内含物」
同根形容词，义为「包含的；范围广的」

senses.title: To have as a part
senses.definition: to have something as one part of a larger whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为较大整体的一部分而存在
senses.example: The price includes breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 价格含早餐。
senses.why: A whole circle drawn around items makes them part of one set.
senses.whyCN: 画一个圈把项目圈进来，它们就成了同一集合的一部分。

senses.title: To count someone in
senses.definition: to make someone or something part of a group or list
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物成为群体或清单的一部分
senses.example: Please include me in the game.
senses.exampleCN: 请把我也算进这场游戏。
senses.why: The circle widens to take in one more member.
senses.whyCN: 圈扩大一点，把又一名成员收进来。

senses.title: Contain as contents
senses.definition: to contain something inside, as a box holds its contents
senses.definitionCN: 像盒子装东西一样把某物含在里面
senses.example: The kit includes a small screwdriver.
senses.exampleCN: 工具包里有一把小螺丝刀。
senses.why: What the box holds is what it includes.
senses.whyCN: 盒子里装着的，就是它所包含的。

senses.title: Including: preposition use
senses.definition: used before a noun to say it is part of a larger amount
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示其属于更大的数量
senses.example: Everyone was there, including the teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 所有人都在，包括老师。
senses.why: The same circle idea turns into a pointing word.
senses.whyCN: 同一个圈的概念转成一个指认词。

intro.en: Include comes from Latin includere, from in- (in) + claudere (to shut, close). The original picture is to shut something in, like closing a door around it.
intro.cn: include 来自拉丁语 includere，由 in-「在内」+ claudere「关闭」构成，本义是「关在里面」，像用门把东西围住。

items.en: Latin claudere meant to shut or close; the root also gave close and claustrophobia.
items.cn: 拉丁语 claudere 意为关闭；同一词根还给了 close 与 claustrophobia。

items.en: in- plus claudere formed includere: to shut in, to enclose.
items.cn: in- 加 claudere 构成 includere：关入、围住。

items.en: In medieval use includere could mean to block in or to contain in writing.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中 includere 可指围堵，也可指写进文中。

items.en: The word passed through Old French forms before reaching English.
items.cn: 该词经古法语形式传入英语。

items.en: Middle English includen first meant to enclose or shut in physically.
items.cn: 中古英语 includen 最初指物理上的围住、关住。

items.en: Modern English softened it to mean simply to have as a part.
items.cn: 现代英语将其弱化为「作为一部分而包含」。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the close-root family. The meaning group compares words about containing parts.
note.cn: 形近组收录含「关闭」词根的词族；词义组比较表示「包含部分」的词。

entries.definition: the noun for the act of including.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指包含这一行为。

entries.definition: covering everything in a range.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖范围内一切的形容词。

entries.definition: to end or decide, from the same root claudere.
entries.definitionCN: 结束或下结论，同出于词根 claudere。

entries.definition: to hold inside, often about contents.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳在内，多指内容物。

entries.definition: to make something a necessary part.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为必要部分。

entries.definition: to consist of the listed parts.
entries.definitionCN: 由所列各部分构成。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the shut-in root, the price phrase and the including trap.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩利用「关进去」的词根、价格短语与 including 的用法。

normal.en: in- plus claudere (close): shut something inside.
normal.cn: in- 加 claudere（关）：把东西关在里面。

normal.en: The price includes tax: the circle already holds it.
normal.cn: the price includes tax：圈里已经装着它。

normal.en: Conclusion and include share one root about closing.
normal.cn: conclusion 与 include 共享一个关于「关闭」的词根。

normal.en: Everyone was there, including the teacher: one pointing word.
normal.cn: including the teacher：一个指认全体的介词。

normal.en: Exclude is the twin: shut out instead of shut in.
normal.cn: exclude 是反义孪生词：关出去而非关进来。

abstract.en: One image: drawing a circle around toys so all belong.
abstract.cn: 只记一个画面：围着玩具画圈，圈内的都算数。

abstract.en: Include is an open door pulled inward.
abstract.cn: include 是一扇被往里拉开的门。

abstract.en: The bigger the circle, the more it includes.
abstract.cn: 圈越大，装得越多。

examples.en: The ticket price includes the museum tour.
examples.cn: 票价包含博物馆参观。

examples.en: Please include your name at the top of the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格顶部写上你的名字。

examples.en: Ten people came, including two new students.
examples.cn: 来了十个人，包括两名新生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「隐克鲁德」：隐在克鲁德圈里的都被包含， include。

root: 拉丁语 in-「在内」+ claudere「关闭」→ includere「关入、围住」→ 古法语 → 中古英语 includen → 现代英语 include；同根词 conclude、disclose、closet。

sensesIntro.en: Include draws a circle: parts inside a whole, names inside a list, and the preposition that points at what the circle holds.
sensesIntro.cn: include 画一个圈：整体内的部分、名单内的名字，以及指向圈内内容的介词。

core.en: A drawn circle that makes whatever it holds count as part of the whole.
core.cn: 一个画出来的圈，圈住的东西都算整体的一部分。

branches.en: PARTHOOD: the price includes breakfast.
branches.cn: 整体与部分：价格含早餐。

branches.en: MEMBERSHIP: include me in the game.
branches.cn: 成员资格：把我也算进游戏。

branches.en: CONTENTS: the kit includes a screwdriver.
branches.cn: 内容物：工具包含螺丝刀。

branches.en: POINTING: including the teacher.
branches.cn: 指认：包括老师。

branches.en: RANGE: what the circle takes in.
branches.cn: 范围：圈所收进的东西。

intro.en: Include builds included, including, inclusion and the opposite exclude.
intro.cn: include 构成 included、including、inclusion 及反义词 exclude。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries show the shutting root claudere and its family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁条目展示「关闭」词根 claudere 及其同族词。

items.example: Lunch is included in the fee.
Many cars passed, including a bus.
items.exampleCN: 许多车驶过，包括一辆巴士。

items.example: The fee is inclusive of meals.
The towels are in the closet.

definition_zh: 不利条件；劣势；缺点；损害
definition_en: an unfavourable condition, or something that causes problems
core_image: 赛跑时比别人多背一个沉重的书包
scene: 班里的辩论赛上，大家分析利弊。 The biggest disadvantage of walking to school is getting wet on rainy days.
sceneCN: 这里 disadvantage 是「不利条件」（第 1 个义项：不好的方面）；句意是步行上学最大的坏处是雨天会淋湿。

derivatives.zh: disadvantage 的词基，义为「优势；有利条件」
过去分词作形容词，义为「处于不利地位的」
advantage 加后缀构成，义为「有利的」

senses.title: An unfavourable condition
senses.definition: something that makes success less likely
senses.definitionCN: 使成功可能性降低的因素
senses.example: Not having a computer at home is a disadvantage for the online class.
senses.exampleCN: 家里没有电脑，上网课就不方便，这是一种劣势。
senses.why: Advantage comes from ahead (abante); dis- turns it around, so disadvantage is being held back.
senses.whyCN: advantage 本义「领先」，加 dis- 便成了「被拖后」。

senses.title: A fault or a problem
senses.definition: a bad point of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物不好的一面
senses.example: Every plan has disadvantages, so we must compare them first.
senses.exampleCN: 每个方案都有缺点，所以要先作比较。
senses.why: What holds one back is also a fault of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 拖人后腿的因素同时也是事物自身的毛病。

intro.en: Disadvantage is advantage wearing the prefix dis-.
intro.cn: disadvantage 是 advantage 加上前缀 dis-。

items.en: Old French avant meant before or ahead, from Latin abante.
items.cn: 古法语 avant 意为在前面，出自拉丁语 abante。

items.en: English built advantage, meaning a position ahead of others.
items.cn: 中古英语构成 advantage，指领先的地位。

items.en: The prefix dis- (against, apart) made disadvantage in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪加上 dis-（相反、分离）构成 disadvantage。

items.en: It named both bad conditions in life and faults of things.
items.cn: 它既指生活中的不利境况，也指事物的缺陷。

items.en: School essays often ask for the advantages and disadvantages of a plan.
items.cn: 学校作文常要求分析某个方案的利与弊。

note.en: These words stand in the better-or-worse field.
note.cn: 这些词属于优劣比较义场。

entries.definition: a good position
entries.definitionCN: 优势

entries.definition: adjective: in a bad position
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：处于不利地位的

entries.definition: helpful, favourable
entries.definitionCN: 有利的

entries.definition: a good viewpoint
entries.definitionCN: 优势位置

entries.definition: to move ahead
entries.definitionCN: 前进

entries.definition: a bad point
entries.definitionCN: 缺点

entries.definition: a poor quality

definition_zh: 实现；达到；取得；完成
definition_en: to succeed in doing something after effort, or to reach a goal
core_image: 运动员冲过终点线
scene: 运动会上，选手全力冲过终点线。 She achieved her best time in the final race.
sceneCN: 这里 achieved 是「取得」（第 1 个义项：经过努力做成某事）；句意为她在决赛中跑出了自己的最好成绩。

pos.zh: 动词：实现；达到；取得；完成

senses.title: To reach a goal
senses.definition: to succeed in reaching a goal
senses.definitionCN: 成功地到达目标
senses.example: We achieved our goal before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在中午前达到了目标。
senses.why: Achieve comes from Old French achever, to finish or to come to a head, so it first means reaching the end of a goal.
senses.whyCN: achieve 来自古法语 achever「完成、到达终点」，本义是把目标走到头。

senses.title: To gain a result by effort
senses.definition: to get a result through work
senses.definitionCN: 通过努力得到某种结果
senses.example: She achieved high marks in the test.
senses.exampleCN: 她在测验中取得了高分。
senses.why: Reaching an end was applied to results, so the word came to mean gaining marks or success.
senses.whyCN: 把「走到终点」用在结果上，就指靠努力取得分数或成功。

senses.title: To complete a task
senses.definition: to finish a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 把一项工作做完
senses.example: The team achieved the work on time.
senses.exampleCN: 团队按时完成了工作。
senses.why: The oldest sense of finishing shows plainly when the object is a piece of work.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是一项工作时，最古老的「完成」义就清楚地显现出来。

intro.en: The recorded history of achieve is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 achieve 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Achever meant to finish or to bring to a head.
items.cn: achever 意为完成或做到头。

items.en: The parts meant to and head, so the verb pictured reaching the top.
items.cn: 其成分意为「向」与「头」，动词描绘到达顶端。

items.en: English borrowed the verb for finishing a task.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪借入这个动词，指完成一项任务。

items.en: The word later took on the sense of gaining a result by effort.
items.cn: 这个词后来带上靠努力获得结果的意思。

items.en: Today it covers goals, dreams and results alike.
items.cn: 今天它可指目标、梦想与各种结果。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definition: The noun for a result gained by effort.

entries.definition: It stresses finishing a task completely.

entries.definition: It stresses reaching a high level or goal.

entries.definition: The plain word for getting to a point or a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 指到达某一点或目标的朴素用词。

normal.cn: a- 表示向，chief 表示头：achieve 就是把事情做到头。

normal.en: The same family also gives achievement and achiever.

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase achieve a goal.

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of achieve in order.

normal.en: Use it when you mean: to succeed in doing something after effort, or to reach a goal.

definition_zh: 百分比；百分之……
definition_en: one part in every hundred; expressed in hundredths
core_image: 把整体切成一百份，取其中若干份的比例尺
scene: 商场周年庆，店员指着海报向顾客说明折扣幅度。 The shop offered a discount of twenty percent on all shoes during the anniversary sale.
sceneCN: 这里 percent 是「百分比」（第 1 个义项：每一百份中的份额）；句意是周年庆期间所有鞋子打八折。

derivatives.zh: percent 加名词后缀 -age 构成，指「百分比；比例；比率」
percent 加 -ile 构成统计学术语，指「百分位数」

senses.title: A part of a hundred
senses.titleCN: 百分比；每一百份中的份额
senses.definition: one part in or for every hundred; a rate expressed in hundredths
senses.definitionCN: 每一百份中的一份或若干份；以百分数表示的比率
senses.example: Ten percent of the students failed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 百分之十的学生没通过考试。
senses.why: Latin per centum literally means for each hundred, so the word itself fixes the whole at one hundred.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 per centum 字面意思是「每一百」，所以这个词本身就把整体锁定为一百份。

senses.title: Percentage in general
senses.definition: a share or proportion of a whole, used loosely without a specific number
senses.definitionCN: 整体中的一部分或比例，泛指时不带具体数字
senses.example: A large percent of his income goes to rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他收入的很大一部分用于房租。
senses.why: When the hundred-part scale becomes a loose share of a whole, the concrete measure turns into an ordinary proportion.
senses.whyCN: 当一百份的刻度被泛化成整体的份额，具体的度量就变成普通的「比例」。

intro.en: Percent is a compressed Latin phrase that became an everyday English noun.
intro.cn: percent 是一个被压缩成日常名词的拉丁语短语。

items.en: The phrase per centum meant for each hundred, combining per (through, by) and centum (hundred).
items.cn: 拉丁短语 per centum 意为「每一百」，由 per（通过、按）和 centum（百）构成。

items.en: In commercial and tax records of medieval Europe, per centum was the standard way to state rates and interest.
items.cn: 中世纪欧洲的商业与税赋记录中，per centum 是表示利率、税率的标准写法。

items.en: Italian merchants used per cento, a shortened form, in account books of trading cities.
items.cn: 意大利商人在账簿中使用缩短的形式 per cento。

items.en: French adopted pour cent, keeping the same structure as business and finance spread.
items.cn: 随着商业金融扩散，法语吸收为 pour cent，结构不变。

items.en: English took over the phrase as per cent in the sixteenth century; the solid spelling percent arose in American usage and is now standard in the United States.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收短语 per cent；连写 percent 起于美式用法，如今是美国的标准拼法。

note.en: Words nearby percent differ in spelling, source, or range of use.
note.cn: 与 percent 相近的词在拼写、来源或使用范围上有差别。

normal.cn: 词根 cent 来自 centum（百），也出现在 century、centimeter。

abstract.en: Feel the crowd split into hundred tiny groups, each group one percent of the whole.

sensesIntro.en: Suggest means to propose an idea, hint at something, or indicate.
sensesIntro.cn: suggest 表示提出想法、暗示某事，或表明。

core.en: Placing an idea where others can see it.
core.cn: 把一个想法放到别人看得见的地方。

branches.en: She suggested that we leave early.
branches.cn: 她建议我们早点出发。

branches.en: He suggested that the plan might fail.

branches.en: The evidence suggests a change.
branches.cn: 证据表明发生了变化。

branches.en: A direct idea and an indirect one both come forward.
branches.cn: 直接的想法和间接的想法都会被摆出来。

definition_zh: 显示器；监测仪；班长；监督者；监测；监控；监听
definition_en: a device that displays or records information, a person who warns or keeps order, or to watch and check something continuously over time
core_image: 一个站在旁边不断提醒“注意”的人，眼睛一直盯着同一处
scene: 控制室里，工程师盯着显示管道压力的监视器。 From the control room the engineer watched the monitor that showed the pressure inside the pipeline.
sceneCN: 这里 monitor 是「显示器」（第 1 个义项：显示画面或数据的屏幕）；句意：工程师在控制室里盯着显示管道内压力的显示器。场景要点：昏暗的控制室、一排亮着的屏幕、屏幕上跳动的压力曲线、管道剖面图；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 显示器；监测仪；班长；监督者；告诫者
监测；监控；监听；跟踪观察

senses.title: A screen that shows the picture
senses.definition: a screen, especially a computer or television display, that shows information or a picture
senses.definitionCN: 显示信息或画面的屏幕，尤指电脑或电视显示屏
senses.example: The second monitor shows the camera feed from the front door.
senses.exampleCN: 第二块显示器显示前门的摄像头画面。
senses.why: Broadcasting used a monitor for a device that continuously checked a transmission, and the screen showing that check took the name. A computer display repeats the role: it lets someone keep watch on what the machine is doing.
senses.whyCN: 广播业曾把持续检查传输质量的设备称为 monitor，显示这项检查的屏幕便沿用了这个名字。电脑显示器重复着同一角色：让人持续看清机器在做什么。

senses.title: An instrument that keeps watch
senses.definition: a device that continuously measures and displays a physical condition, such as heart rate or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 持续测量并显示某项身体或物理状况的设备，如心率或压力
senses.example: The heart monitor began to beep faster and faster.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏监测仪开始越响越快地鸣叫。
senses.why: The Latin monitor was a person who warned. An instrument that watches a pulse and sounds an alarm takes over the warning job, so the person's title passes to the machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 是一个发出警告的人。一台盯着脉搏、并发出警报的仪器接过了这份警告的职责，于是人的称呼转移到了机器上。

senses.title: The pupil who keeps order
senses.definition: a senior pupil at a school given the task of keeping order or checking attendance
senses.definitionCN: 学校里被赋予维持秩序或检查出勤任务的高年级学生
senses.example: The hall monitor checked the corridors every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 走廊值日生每小时巡查一次走廊。
senses.why: This is the oldest English sense, from 1540s: a senior pupil 'charged with keeping order'. The student does exactly what the Latin word says — reminds others of the rules and reports breaches.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最古老的义项，始于 16 世纪 40 年代：受命维持秩序的高年级学生。这个学生做的正是拉丁词所说的——提醒别人守规矩，并报告违规。

senses.title: An official who warns
senses.definition: a person appointed to observe, advise, and warn, especially in an official or technical role
senses.definitionCN: 受指派观察、建议并提出告诫的人，尤指担任正式或技术职务者
senses.example: A monitor was appointed to warn the committee about conflicts of interest.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会任命了一名监督员，就利益冲突提出告诫。
senses.why: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide'. The English noun keeps that advisory, warning figure before it ever names a machine.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人”。英语名词先保留了这个提出建议与警告的人，之后才用它命名机器。

senses.title: Watch the numbers over time
senses.definition: to measure and check a quantity or condition regularly over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内定期测量并检查某个数量或状况
senses.example: Sensors monitor the temperature of the tank every ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器每十分钟监测一次储罐的温度。
senses.why: The verb appeared in 1924 for checking the quality of radio signals. Its core is repetition: a monitor does not look once but keeps looking, so the verb means sustained checking rather than a single glance.
senses.whyCN: 动词于 1924 年出现，指检查无线电信号的质量。它的核心是重复：monitor 不是看一眼，而是持续地看，所以这个动词表示持续的检查，而不是一瞥。

senses.title: Keep someone under surveillance
senses.definition: to watch a person, group, or activity closely, especially to detect wrongdoing or risk
senses.definitionCN: 密切注视某人、某群体或某项活动，尤为了发现不当行为或风险
senses.example: The company monitors its drivers' speed and braking through an app.
senses.exampleCN: 公司通过一个应用监控司机的车速与刹车情况。
senses.why: When the watching is turned from a gauge to people, the warning role becomes surveillance. The same continuous attention is now aimed at behaviour that may need correcting.
senses.whyCN: 当注视的对象从仪表转向人，提醒的职责就变成了监控。同样的持续关注，现在对准了可能需要纠正的行为。

senses.title: Listen to a channel
senses.definition: to listen to a radio, telephone, or other channel continuously in order to catch particular information
senses.definitionCN: 持续收听无线电、电话或其他频道，以捕捉特定信息
senses.example: They monitored the radio channel all night, waiting for a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 他们整夜监听那个无线电频道，等待回复。
senses.why: The earliest verb sense was exactly this: checking radio signals for quality. Listening to a channel is watching with the ears, and the word's continuity remains.
senses.whyCN: 最早的动词义正是这个：检查无线电信号的质量。用耳朵听一个频道就是“用耳朵看”，而这个词的持续性仍然保留。

senses.title: The lizard that warns
senses.definition: a large lizard of the family Varanidae, called a monitor because of an old story that it warned people of crocodiles
senses.definitionCN: 巨蜥科的大型蜥蜴，因古老传说称它会向人预警鳄鱼而得名
senses.example: A monitor lizard crossed the trail and disappeared into the grass.
senses.exampleCN: 一只巨蜥穿过小径，消失在草丛里。
senses.why: The name was given in 1826 because the lizard was fabled to give warning of Nile crocodiles. It is the same 'warner' sense, applied to an animal rather than a person or device.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字始于 1826 年，因为传说这种蜥蜴会预警尼罗河鳄鱼。它仍是“警告者”这层意思，只是用在了动物身上，而不是人或设备。

senses.title: The ironclad that admonished
senses.definition: the name of the first ironclad warship of that design, built in 1862 and intended as a warning to the Confederacy
senses.definitionCN: 1862 年建造的第一艘该型铁甲舰的名称，意在向南方邦联发出警告
senses.example: The Monitor fought the Merrimack in 1862 and changed naval warfare.
senses.exampleCN: 1862 年，莫尼特号与梅里马克号交战，改变了海战方式。
senses.why: The inventor chose the name because the ship was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders. The Latin warner becomes a floating threat, a warning made of iron.
senses.whyCN: 发明者选择这个名字，是因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。拉丁语的告诫者变成了浮在水上的威胁，一个用铁铸成的警告。

senses.title: A background watcher in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的后台监控程序
senses.definition: in computing, a program or process that runs in the background and checks system activity
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，指在后台运行、检查系统活动的程序或进程
senses.example: A background monitor logs every login and flags unusual hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一个后台监控程序记录每次登录，并标记异常时段。
senses.why: Software repeats the human watchman: it runs unnoticed, checks continuously, and reports what looks wrong. The old 'one who warns' is now a loop of code.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复着人类更夫的角色：它不声不响地运行，持续检查，并报告看起来不对的地方。古老的“告诫者”如今成了一段循环的代码。

intro.en: Monitor began as a Latin word for a person who warns, entered English in the sixteenth century as a school officer, and only in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries became a machine, a lizard, a warship, and finally a screen. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monitor 最初是拉丁语中表示“告诫者”的词，16 世纪作为学校职务进入英语，直到 19 与 20 世纪才变成仪器、蜥蜴、军舰，最后成为屏幕。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as 'senior pupil at a school charged with keeping order'. It came from Latin monitor.
items.cn: 英语最早记录为“受命维持秩序的学校高年级学生”。它来自拉丁语 monitor。

items.en: Latin monitor meant 'one who reminds, admonishes, or checks', and also 'an overseer, instructor, guide, teacher'. It was an agent noun from monere.
items.cn: 拉丁语 monitor 意为“提醒者、告诫者、检查者”，也指“监督者、指导者、引路人、教师”。它是 monere 的施动名词。

items.en: Monere meant 'to remind, bring to one's recollection, tell of; admonish, advise, warn, instruct, teach'. It goes back to PIE *moneie-, a causative form of *men- 'to think', the root also behind Latin memini 'I remember' and mens 'mind'.
items.cn: monere 意为“提醒、使想起、告知；告诫、建议、警告、指导、教导”。它可追溯到原始印欧语 *moneie-，即 *men-“思考”的使役形式；同一词根也是拉丁语 memini“我记得”与 mens“心智”的来源。

items.en: The monitor lizard was so called because it was fabled to warn people of Nile crocodiles (1826). The ironclad warship Monitor (1862) was named by its inventor because it was meant to 'admonish' Confederate leaders.
items.cn: 巨蜥被称为 monitor，是因为传说它会向人预警尼罗河鳄鱼（1826）。铁甲舰莫尼特号（1862）由发明者命名，因为这艘船意在“告诫”南方邦联的领导人。

items.en: The verb is recorded in 1924 meaning 'to check for quality', originally of radio signals. The general sense 'observe, keep under review' is from 1944. Keats had used it in 1818 to mean 'to guide'.
items.cn: 动词于 1924 年有记录，意为“检查质量”，最初用于无线电信号。泛指“观察、持续审视”的义项始于 1944 年。济慈在 1818 年曾用它表示“引导”。

items.en: A broadcasting sense, 'a device to continuously check on the technical quality of a transmission', is recorded from 1931 and led to the sense 'a TV screen displaying the picture from a particular camera'. The computer display is a later extension of that screen sense.
items.cn: 广播义“持续检查传输技术质量的设备”记录于 1931 年，并由此引出“显示某一摄像机画面的电视屏幕”这一义项。电脑显示器是该屏幕义的后期引申。

note.en: The first group separates the noun and adjective forms built on monitor from two related warning words; the second compares the verbs of watching that learners use interchangeably.
note.cn: 第一组把由 monitor 构成的名词与形容词形式，同两个相关的“警告”词分开；第二组比较学习者常互换使用的几个“看管”动词。

entries.definition: the continuous act of checking or watching something. It is the process, while monitor is the device or the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 持续检查或观察的行为。它是过程，而 monitor 是设备或动词。

entries.definition: giving or serving as a warning. It keeps the Latin sense of admonition and is mostly formal.
entries.definitionCN: 给予警告的，或起警告作用的。它保留了拉丁语“告诫”的意思，多用于正式语境。

entries.definition: to warn or reprimand someone firmly but not harshly. It shares the Latin monere root but is a separate verb, not a form of monitor.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定但不严厉地警告或责备某人。它与 monitor 共享拉丁语 monere 词根，但它是另一个动词，不是 monitor 的词形。

entries.definition: a feeling that something is about to happen, especially something bad. It is a warning that comes before the event, built with pre- 'before'.
entries.definitionCN: 一种某事即将发生、尤指坏事的感觉。它是事件之前到来的警告，由 pre-“在前”构成。

entries.definition: to be in charge of people or work and make sure it is done properly. It stresses authority over workers, while monitor stresses continuous checking of signals or conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 负责管理人或工作，确保事情做好。它强调对工作者的权威，而 monitor 强调对信号或状况的持续检查。

entries.definition: to look at something for a period of time, often without measuring it. Monitor usually adds a purpose: to detect change, risk, or poor quality.
entries.definitionCN: 在一段时间内看着某物，通常不进行测量。monitor 通常多一层目的：发现变化、风险或质量问题。

entries.definition: to follow the movement or development of something over time, often by recorded traces. It focuses on where something goes; monitor focuses on whether it stays within limits.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间跟踪某物的移动或发展，常依据记录下来的痕迹。它关注东西去了哪里，monitor 关注它是否仍在限度之内。

entries.definition: to examine people, substances, or signals in order to sort or filter them. It is usually a test applied at a point in time, while monitor is a watch kept over time.
entries.definitionCN: 检查人、物质或信号，以便分类或筛选。它通常是在某一时点施行的检验，而 monitor 是长期保持的观察。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin monere 'warn', the agent noun monitor, and the English family monitoring, monitory, admonish, and premonition.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 monere“警告”、施动名词 monitor，以及英语词族 monitoring、monitory、admonish、premonition。

normal.en: monere means 'to warn, remind'. A monitor is literally 'one who warns' — first a pupil, then an instrument, then a screen.
normal.cn: monere 意为“警告、提醒”。monitor 字面上就是“发出警告的人”——先是学生，再是仪器，最后是屏幕。

normal.en: The school sense is the oldest English one (1540s); the machine and screen senses are centuries later.
normal.cn: 学校职务义是英语里最古老的义项（16 世纪 40 年代）；仪器与屏幕义要晚好几个世纪。

normal.en: The verb arrived in 1924 for checking radio signal quality, which is why 'monitor a channel' still sounds natural.
normal.cn: 动词于 1924 年出现，用于检查无线电信号质量，所以 monitor a channel 至今听起来自然。

normal.en: monitoring is the process, monitory is 'warning', admonish is a separate verb from the same root.
normal.cn: monitoring 是过程，monitory 是“警告的”，admonish 则是同根的另一动词。

normal.en: A monitor differs from a supervisor: it keeps checking a signal or condition, while a supervisor holds authority over people.
normal.cn: monitor 与 supervisor 不同：它持续检查信号或状况，而 supervisor 对人拥有管理权。

abstract.en: Picture a night watchman at a factory gate. He does not repair anything; he looks, checks, and raises the alarm.
abstract.cn: 想象一名守在工厂大门的更夫。他不修理任何东西；他看、检查、发出警报。

abstract.en: Move that watchman into a box on the wall, and he becomes a heart monitor; put his gaze on a screen, and he becomes a display.
abstract.cn: 把这位更夫装进墙上的盒子，他就成了心脏监测仪；把他的目光放到屏幕上，他就成了显示器。

abstract.en: The word always means attention spread over time: a single look is not monitoring, however careful it is.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终表示铺在时间上的注意：只看一眼，无论多仔细，都不算监测。

examples.en: Nurses monitor the patient's pulse and blood pressure every hour.
examples.cn: 护士每小时监测病人的脉搏与血压。

examples.en: The app monitors how much time you spend on each website.
examples.cn: 这个应用监控你在每个网站上花多少时间。

examples.en: The teacher left a monitor in charge of the class while she fetched the keys.
examples.cn: 老师去取钥匙时，让班长负责管班。

dict_mnemonic.text: “莫离他”——莫要离开他，他一直在旁边盯着、随时提醒你 → monitor 监视器；监测（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 monere“警告、提醒”的施动名词 monitor“告诫者”，核心是“持续盯着并随时发出提醒”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of monitor, all held together by one figure: someone standing beside a thing, watching without stopping and speaking up when something is wrong.
sensesIntro.cn: monitor 的十个义项都由同一个形象串起：有人站在某物旁边，不停地看，一有不对就出声提醒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warner standing beside, eyes fixed on one spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个站在旁边、目光钉在一处的告诫者。

branches.en: INSTRUMENTS: the warner becomes a measuring device, and the screen that shows its check takes the same name.
branches.cn: 仪器：告诫者变成测量设备，显示这项检查的屏幕也沿用了同一个名字。

branches.en: PEOPLE: the oldest senses keep a person in the role, either a pupil keeping order or an official who warns.
branches.cn: 人：最古老的义项让一个人留在这个角色里，或是维持秩序的学生，或是提出告诫的官员。

branches.en: WATCHING: the verb checks quantities over time, and when aimed at people it becomes surveillance.
branches.cn: 注视：动词随时间检查数量，而当对象转向人时，它就变成监控。

branches.en: LISTENING: a channel is watched with the ears, the earliest verb use of all.
branches.cn: 监听：频道是用耳朵看的，这是所有动词用法中最早的一个。

branches.en: THE NAME TRAVELS: a lizard fabled to warn, an ironclad built to admonish, and a background program that keeps checking.
branches.cn: 名字远行：传说会预警的蜥蜴、为告诫而造的铁甲舰，以及持续检查的后台程序。

intro.en: Monitor is a Latin agent noun in -itor built on mon- 'warn'. English adds -ing, -y, -ial and -ship, while the same root also reaches English through admonish, monition, and premonition.
intro.cn: monitor 是拉丁语中以 -itor 结尾的施动名词，词干 mon- 意为“警告”。英语加上 -ing、-y、-ial 与 -ship，同一词根还通过 admonish、monition、premonition 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is monere 'warn, remind', its agent noun monitor, and the action noun monitio 'a warning'. Summon also belongs here: Latin summonere meant 'hint, remind, warn'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词族包括 monere“警告、提醒”、它的施动名词 monitor，以及行为名词 monitio“警告”。summon 也属于这里：拉丁语 summonere 意为“暗示、提醒、警告”。

items.meaning: one who warns or checks; a checking device
items.meaningCN: 告诫者；检查者；监测设备（mon- 警告 + -itor 施动名词）
items.example: The monitor on the wall showed a steady line.
items.exampleCN: 墙上的监测仪显示出一条平稳的线。

items.meaningCN: 监测；监控（-ing 构成过程名词）
items.example: The patient was kept under close monitoring.
items.exampleCN: 病人被置于密切监测之下。

items.meaningCN: 告诫的；警告的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: He gave a monitory glance at the noisy table.
items.exampleCN: 他朝吵闹的那桌投去一个警告的目光。

items.meaning: relating to a monitor or prefect
items.meaningCN: 级长的；监督的（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: The monitorial duties rotated each week.

items.meaningCN: 告诫；温和地责备（ad- 向 + mon- 警告）
items.example: The coach admonished the players for arriving late.
items.exampleCN: 教练因球员迟到而告诫了他们。

items.example: She ignored the admonition and drove faster.
items.exampleCN: 她无视那句告诫，反而开得更快。

items.meaning: a warning, especially an official one

definition_zh: 胶水；胶黏物；胶合；紧贴不舍（作动词）

senses.title: A sticky joining substance
senses.definition: a thick sticky liquid or paste used for joining surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 用于黏合表面的黏稠液体或膏体
senses.example: A drop of glue sealed the torn page.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴胶水把撕坏的书页封好了。
senses.why: The core image is a liquid that grips two things so hard they will not part.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是把两样东西黏得拆不开的液体。

senses.title: To fasten with glue
senses.definition: to join things together using glue
senses.definitionCN: 用胶水把东西连在一起
senses.example: The pupils glued the paper pieces onto the wheel.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们把纸片粘到风车上。
senses.why: The substance turns into the action: the stickiness does the joining.
senses.whyCN: 物质转为动作：靠黏性完成连接。

senses.title: To fix eyes or attention
senses.definition: to keep eyes or attention firmly fixed on something
senses.definitionCN: 使眼睛或注意力牢牢锁定某物
senses.example: The children were glued to the cartoon show.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们目不转睛地看动画片。

senses.whyCN: 胶水对纸做的事，吸引对眼睛做的事：离不开。

senses.title: Any bonding agent
